cna.title: PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder <= 7.1.1 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection to Remote Code Execution via 'customer_note' Checkout Field

affected.product: PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder

descriptions.value: The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.1 via the 'customer_note' parameter parameter. This is due to insufficient sanitization of the customer_note checkout field, which is inlined verbatim into invoice HTML, entity-decoded back into a live tag by simplehtmldom, reassembled into raw bytes by mPDF, and passed to unserialize() in _getObjAttr without validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger the vulnerable code path on a default install by placing an anonymous WooCommerce checkout via the public Store API (POST /wc/store/v1/checkout) using a Direct Bank Transfer or cheque payment method, which automatically transitions the order to 'on-hold' status and fires the plugin's invoice-generation hook.

cna.title: undici vulnerable to TLS certificate validation bypass via dropped tls options in Agent

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions 4.0.0 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, its Agent dispatcher passes its constructor options through a JSON-based deep clone before forwarding them to each per-origin pool, and because JSON cannot represent functions, a caller-supplied tls option containing a checkServerIdentity callback is silently dropped before it reaches the TLS layer. As a result, a TLS peer whose certificate a custom checkServerIdentity was written to reject, but which passes Node's default hostname and chain checks, is silently accepted. Because Agent is the default dispatcher behind request, fetch, and setGlobalDispatcher, this affects the path most applications use, and EnvHttpProxyAgent is affected on its direct and no-proxy routes as well, while only applications that pass a function-valued tls option such as a custom checkServerIdentity for certificate or public-key pinning are at risk. The issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, and 8.12.2, which preserve the tls option outside the JSON clone so custom verification callbacks are forwarded unchanged, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, pass the TLS options through connect instead of tls, or for proxied destinations use requestTls and proxyTls.

solutions.value: Upgrade to 7.2.0

cna.title: Germanized for WooCommerce <= 4.1.4 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Unauthorized Access of Private Data via Activation Token Reuse via Activation Token Reuse After Email Change

descriptions.value: The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Unauthorized Access of Private Data via Activation Token Reuse in versions up to, and including, 4.1.4. This is due to the `on_user_email_changed` hook — which is responsible for rotating the activation token and recording a pending-email-change marker on an unactivated Customer account — only being registered inside the `is_double_opt_in_login_enabled()` branch when "Disable login for unactivated customers" is set to Yes, leaving the original `?activate=` token valid and entirely unbound to the email address it was issued for when that setting is No. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to change their account email to a victim's billing email via the standard `/my-account/edit-account/` form and then redeem their original activation token through `customer_account_activate()`, triggering `link_customer_past_orders()` to reassign any matching guest order to the attacker's account and exposing the original buyer's billing name, street address, phone number, and purchased items on the attacker's My Account order page. Exploitation requires the site to have double opt-in enabled with "Disable login for unactivated customers" explicitly set to No (a non-default configuration), public customer registration enabled, and the original activation token redeemed within its one-day expiry window.

cna.title: Mang Board - 2.4.4 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via 'image_path' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in version 2.4.4 via the mbw_file_upload function. This is due to missing file extension validation on the attacker-supplied image_path parameter, whose basename-derived file name bypasses the extension allowlist applied only to the separate file_name parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. Exploitation requires the board to be configured to allow guest posts, which is the plugin's default mode; the required nonce is printed on every public board page, making it readable by any unauthenticated visitor without a WordPress login.

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Aisle Research for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value: If VNC is not required, disable the gnome-remote-desktop VNC service. If it must remain enabled, restrict the VNC listener to trusted hosts or management networks using host-based firewall rules.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in gnome-remote-desktop as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. In the VNC TLS read path, partial consumption of the internal peek buffer incorrectly moves remaining peeked bytes into the caller-supplied buffer instead of compacting the peek buffer. A remote attacker who can reach an enabled VNC TLS listener and trigger a peek/read size mismatch can cause an out-of-bounds write, leading to denial of service.

cna.title: undici WebSocket client vulnerable to Denial of Service via unbounded automatic PONG buffering

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions 5.15.0 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, its WebSocket client, including the bundled WebSocket exposed by Node.js, can be driven to exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised WebSocket server. For every PING frame received, the client automatically writes a PONG response and ignores the backpressure signal from the socket write, so a server that streams small PING frames while never reading the client's PONGs makes the outbound write queue and heap grow without bound until the Node.js process runs out of memory and terminates. The attack is remote and unauthenticated, needs only a normal WebSocket connection, and is asymmetric, since small inbound PINGs produce a much larger retained outbound queue, with availability the only impact. The issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, and 8.12.2, which pause WebSocket frame parsing when the automatic PONG response hits socket backpressure and resume on drain, bounding the outbound queue, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. There is no workaround.

cna.title: Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce <= 1.3.0 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass to Account Takeover via Fake Telegram Webhook + Brute-Forced Login Token

descriptions.value: The Bot for Telegram on WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass leading to Account Takeover in all versions up to, and including, 1.3.0. The `/wp-json/woo-telegram/v1/main/` REST endpoint is registered with `permission_callback => '__return_true'` and performs no Telegram webhook signature verification, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to POST a forged bot update with a `message.chat.id` set to any WordPress login name; `bftow_get_user_system_id()` resolves this attacker-supplied value to the targeted account via `get_user_by('login', $tgId)` with no ownership proof, and writes a login token computed as `md5($_SERVER['HTTP_USER_AGENT'] . time())` — both inputs are fully attacker-controlled or bounded within seconds using the response's own `Date` header. The resulting token is redeemable at the unauthenticated, capability-check-free, and nonce-less `?action=bftow_create_order&bftow_token=` endpoint, which calls `wp_set_auth_cookie()` unconditionally via `login_user_by_id`, issuing a persistent authenticated session cookie for the targeted account to the attacker. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as any WordPress user, including administrators, given only that user's username.

This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is triggered specifically when the victim clicks the embedded document's Download button, which causes the de_track_download AJAX fallback path to programmatically create an anchor with the attacker-controlled href and call .click() — a condition reached because supplying docId=0 causes can_read_document() to return false, bypassing the normal download flow.

cna.title: undici vulnerable to Denial of Service via unhandled error on excessive content-encodings

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions 6.23.0 through 6.29.0, 7.18.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, its fetch() implementation crashes the Node.js process when a malicious server returns a response with more than five content codings and closes the connection before sending the body. undici rejects such responses because of a content-encoding limit, but it created the internal response stream before that check and returned without attaching an error listener or aborting the request, so the early close surfaces a content-length mismatch on the orphaned stream, which Node.js treats as an unhandled error and terminates the process. A remote, unauthenticated server can trigger this with a single response, even when the application correctly catches the fetch() rejection, resulting in a denial of service. The issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, and 8.12.2, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. There is no workaround.

cna.title: Aliro ValidityIteration check bypassed for certificate-trusted Credential Issuer (fail open)

credits.value: Dr. Sayon Duttagupta, COSIC, KU Leuven, Belgium

descriptions.value: CAPEC-255 Subvert Access Control

affected.product: nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on

versions.version: v1.0.0 through v1.1.1 (inclusive). Fixed in v1.2.0.

descriptions.value:
In the Aliro access control reference
  applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control
  Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, built with Credential Issuer CA
  certificate-based issuer trust (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_ISSUER_CA) and
  the Aliro Step-up phase (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE) enabled,
  AccessManagerImpl::ProcessValidityIteration() treats a failed lookup of the
  Credential Issuer in the provisioned issuer array as success. For an issuer
  trusted through a certificate chain but not provisioned, the
  ValidityIteration (credential-rollback) check is therefore skipped. A former
  authorized holder with an old but correctly issuer-signed Access Document can
  be granted physical access after the issuer has advanced its iteration to
  revoke that credential. The default Matter provisioning configuration is not
  affected. Fixed in v1.2.0.

supportingMedia.value: In the Aliro access control reference applications of the Nordic Semiconductor nRF Door Lock and Access Control Add-on v1.0.0 through v1.1.1, built with Credential Issuer CA certificate-based issuer trust (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_ISSUER_CA) and the Aliro Step-up phase (CONFIG_DOOR_LOCK_STEP_UP_PHASE) enabled, AccessManagerImpl::ProcessValidityIteration() treats a failed lookup of the Credential Issuer in the provisioned issuer array as success. For an issuer trusted through a certificate chain but not provisioned, the ValidityIteration (credential-rollback) check is therefore skipped. cna.title: OpenStation: Desktop Windows, Dock & Virtual Desktops for WP Admin <= 1.1.16 - Missing Authorization to Authenticated (Subscriber+) Arbitrary Placement Modification and Entity Metadata Disclosure via PATCH /files/placements/<id> on orphaned placements

affected.product: OpenStation – Admin Dashboard Notes, Custom Dashboard, AI Assistant & PWA

descriptions.value: The OpenStation: Desktop Windows, Dock & Virtual Desktops for WP Admin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.16. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to modify arbitrary other users' placement rows (position, sort order, parent folder, and meta) and read serialized metadata — including title, permalink, and post status — of the entities those orphaned placements reference. cna.title: Symfony: Unbounded Nesting in the Expression Parser Lets Untrusted Expressions Crash the Process

descriptions.value:
In Symfony Expression Language versions prior to 5.4.54, 6.4.48, 7.4.21, and 8.1.9, the parser of the ExpressionLanguage component built its node tree with no bound on its depth. An expression made of tens of thousands of nested unary operators, array literals, binary operators or property accesses crashed the PHP process, while the tree was being freed.


#[Assert\ExpressionSyntax] passes the validated value to ExpressionLanguage::lint(), so an application validating expressions written by its users could be crashed by a single request, and so could any code parsing untrusted expressions.

This issue affects symfony/expression-language through v5.4.53, v6.0.0-BETA1 through v6.4.47, v7.0.0-BETA1 through v7.4.20, and v8.0.0-BETA1 through v8.1.8.

cna.title: Symfony: Unbounded Recursion in the YAML Inline Lexer Lets a Single Document Crash the Process

descriptions.value:
In Symfony YAML prior to versions 5.4.54, 6.4.45, 7.4.18, and 8.1.6, Yaml\Parser::lexInlineStructure() recursed through lexInlineMapping() and lexInlineSequence() for every { and [ of an inline collection, without entering the nesting level that the rest of the parser bounds with maxNestingLevel. A document made of deeply nested inline collections, such as [[[[...]]]], exhausted the stack while it was being lexed: depending on the PHP version and its stack settings, the process crashed or the request ended with a fatal error.



Any code parsing untrusted YAML is affected. That includes #[MapRequestPayload] when the Yaml component is installed and the endpoint does not restrict acceptFormat: a single unauthenticated request with a YAML content type is enough.



This issue affects symfony/yaml through v5.4.53, v6.0.0-BETA1 through v6.4.44, v7.0.0-BETA1 through v7.4.17, and v8.0.0-BETA1 through v8.1.5.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Data collection. Tidewave.tidewave_config_meta/1 builds a map with root (Tidewave.MCP.root()), framework.app_paths (Mix.Project.deps_paths()), wsl_distro, and host_path. It HTML-escapes the JSON encoding of the map into <meta name="tidewave:config">.

2. Exposure. Tidewave.Router.control_html/1 serves the tag on GET /tidewave/connect. For all other routes, Tidewave.call/2 registers a before_send callback that injects the tag into every text/html response when toolbar: true.

3. Read access. check_origin/2 accepts any request without an Origin header, and no code validates Host. After DNS rebinding, the browser sends a same-origin GET from a loopback peer.

**2. Exposure.** `Tidewave.Router.control_html/1` serves the tag on `GET /tidewave/connect`. For all other routes, `Tidewave.call/2` registers a `before_send` callback that injects the tag into every `text/html` response when `toolbar: true`.

cna.title: Apache Syncope: Remote Code Execution via Flowable JUEL expression

descriptions.value:
Improper isolation or compartmentalization vulnerability in Apache Syncope.

An administrator with adequate entitlements can import arbitrary BPMN process definitions via the REST API and then start the process. When a BPMN process containing a JUEL expression is imported and started, the expression is executed directly on the server, with no sandbox.



This issue affects Apache Syncope: from 3.0.0-M0 through 3.0.16, from 4.0.0-M0 through 4.0.8, from 4.1.0 through 4.1.3.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 4.0.9 / 4.1.4, which fix this issue by rejecting BPMN definitions including expression attributes.

cna.title: Authentication Bypass in CAST Imaging

descriptions.value:
CAST Imaging is vulnerable to authentication bypass in the TenantFilter class. The TenantFilter processes the X-ISSUER-LOCATION HTTP header and dynamically registers an OpenID Connect issuer based on its value. An unauthenticated remote attacker can register a malicious identity provider, create users matching existing administrative usernames, and obtain valid JWTs which will be accepted by the application. This results in complete authentication bypass and privilege escalation to administrative access.




The vulnerability has only been confirmed in version 3.6.2 but may also affect other versions. The vendor did not provide the affected version range, but assured that the vulnerability is fixed "in newer versions".

cna.title: Clevis: clevis: pkcs#11 token pin written to world-readable file

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Sergio Correia (Red Hat).

workarounds.value:
Configure the clevis-luks-pkcs11-askpass systemd service with a restrictive UMask by creating a service override using systemctl edit. Setting UMask to 0077 prevents the PIN file from being readable by non-root users.

This workaround only covers the systemd service path. The dracut initramfs code path is not covered by this mitigation.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the clevis PKCS#11 pin. The clevis-luks-pkcs11-askpin script writes the PKCS#11 token PIN in plaintext to a file without setting restrictive permissions. Under the default process umask, the file is world-readable. Additionally, the PIN file is not reliably cleaned up if the decryption script exits early, leaving the PIN accessible indefinitely.

descriptions.value:
CAST Imaging has multiple path traversal vulnerabilities in various endpoints. The application does not properly validate the path parameters, allowing an authenticated attacker to use "../" sequences to escape the intended directory and read arbitrary files.


Critically, by reading "/proc/self/environ", the attacker can obtain environment variables containing sensitive credentials such as Keycloak and PostgreSQL passwords, leading to full server compromise and administrative access.

Reject long URLs before parsing them, for example anything above a few kilobytes, and reject a parsed `port` above 65535 before rendering or using the `%URI{}`. `URI.new/1` is not affected on Erlang/OTP 27.3.4.17, 28.5.0.6, 29.0.6 and later, where `:uri_string` limits the port to 5 digits.

descriptions.value:
Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the Elixir standard library's URI module allows an attacker who supplies a URL to cause a denial of service through CPU exhaustion.

URI.parse/1 converts the port component with String.to_integer/1 in split_authority/1 (lib/elixir/lib/uri.ex) without bounding its length, so a port of up to 1,262,592 decimal digits produces a bignum of that size and a longer one raises SystemLimitError. Rendering the parsed URI back to text (URI.to_string/1, inspect/1, logging, error formatting) converts the bignum with :erlang.integer_to_binary/1, which is quadratic on Erlang/OTP 27, 28 and 29.0: a 400,000-digit port renders in about 2.6 seconds and a 1 MB port in about 18 seconds. Ports above 65535 are also accepted.

This issue affects elixir: from 0.5.0 before 1.18.6, from 1.19.0-rc.0 before 1.19.7, and from 1.20.0-rc.0 before 1.20.5.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Unbounded conversion

split_authority/1 matches the port with the regex (:(\d*))? and converts it with String.to_integer/1. Nothing bounds the digit run, so the VM builds an integer of up to 1,262,592 decimal digits (about 30 ms to parse 400,000 digits) and raises SystemLimitError above that, which escapes URI.parse/1 instead of producing a %URI{}.

2. Render cost

URI.to_string/1 renders the port with Integer.to_string/1, and inspect/1 renders it the same way, both through :erlang.integer_to_binary/1. That conversion is quadratic on OTP 27, 28 and 29.0 and sub-quadratic from OTP 29.1 (https://github.com/erlang/otp/pull/11074). Per GHSA-8qw4-2chm-mvj2 it occupies a dirty CPU scheduler for its full duration.

3. Comparison with URI.new/1

Erlang/OTP limited the port to 5 bytes in :uri_string.parse/1 as part of GHSA-8qw4-2chm-mvj2. URI.new/1 and URI.new!/1 use :uri_string and get that limit on patched OTP versions. URI.parse/1 does its own parsing and does not.

4. Reach

Header-sourced URLs are bounded by HTTP server limits. Form and JSON body fields are not: Plug's default JSON body limit is 8 MB. One observed library path: a user-supplied URL passed to Req inside a Bandit request exits with the port in its arguments, and Bandit's error logging formats it, which took 2.8 seconds at 400,000 digits on OTP 28.

cna.title: The Innovative Form Builder <= 1.5.1 - Authenticated (Custom+) Arbitrary File Upload via 'allowedFileExtensions' Configuration + Public /form/submission/ Multipart Upload

descriptions.value: The The Innovative Form Builder – IvyForms plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.1 via the filterFiletypeAndExt function. This is due to insufficient file type validation due to the absence of a dangerous-extension denylist in the allowed-extensions sanitizer and deliberate override of WordPress's native MIME and extension defences via a registered wp_check_filetype_and_ext filter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with custom-level access and above, to upload files that may be executable, which makes remote code execution possible. An authenticated attacker with the custom add_edit_forms capability must first configure a File Upload field with a dangerous extension (e.g., php) in the allowed-extensions list; once that form is published, any unauthenticated visitor can trigger the actual file upload via the publicly accessible /wp-json/ivyforms/v1/form/submission/ REST route.

cna.title: Clevis: clevis: pkcs#11 luks passphrase logged in plaintext to world-readable file

credits.value: This issue was discovered by Sergio Correia (Red Hat).

workarounds.value:
Configure the clevis-luks-pkcs11-askpass systemd service with a restrictive UMask by creating a service override using systemctl edit. Setting UMask to 0077 prevents the log file from being readable by non-root users. Additionally, remove any existing log files under /run/systemd/clevis-pkcs11-*.log after each boot, as they may already contain passphrases from previous unlocks.

This workaround only covers the systemd service path. The dracut initramfs code path is not covered by this mitigation.

workarounds.value: Check the GitHub Security Advisory for mitigation strategies.

descriptions.value: PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. affected.product: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support

workarounds.value: If VNC is not required, disable the gnome-remote-desktop VNC service. If it must remain enabled, restrict the VNC listener to trusted hosts or management networks using host-based firewall rules.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in gnome-remote-desktop as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. cna.title: Customer Email Verification for WooCommerce <= 2.8.2 - Unauthenticated Authentication Bypass via Predictable Email-Verification Token to 'cusomer_email_verify' Parameter

descriptions.value: The Customer Email Verification for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via a Predictable Email-Verification Token in all versions up to, and including, 2.8.2. This is due to the `authenticate_user_by_email_link()` function — hooked on the `wp` action and triggered by the `cusomer_email_verify` GET parameter — lacking any capability check or nonce verification, while the `secret_code` it validates is generated as `md5(email . time())` and the `verify_otp_nonce` required to trigger token issuance via the `wp_ajax_nopriv_resend_otp` handler is emitted to every front-end visitor through `wp_localize_script`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as a newly created, verified WooCommerce customer bound to an arbitrary email address — or to flip an existing account's `customer_email_verified` meta to verified — fully bypassing the plugin's core email-verification control. Exploitation requires the `cev_user_log` table to contain a `password` column, which is absent from the fresh-install schema shipped in version 2.8.2 but is present on sites upgraded from an older version where that column was defined.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication CIBA implementation within the keycloak-services component of Keycloak. cna.title: Samba: access control bypass via vfs_ceph_rgw case-insensitive open

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank hataehoon for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Only shares configured with the vfs_ceph_rgw module are affected.

To mitigate this vulnerability, disable the experimental `vfs_ceph_rgw` module on any configured Samba shares. Edit `/etc/samba/smb.conf` to remove `ceph_rgw` from the `vfs objects` setting under the relevant share sections, then reload the Samba service:

```
systemctl reload smb
```

Warning: Reloading or restarting the `smb` service may briefly interrupt active client sessions. Additionally, removing this module disables Ceph RGW integration for the affected shares.

Setting ```case sensitive = yes``` on affected shares avoids the vulnerability, because the differently-cased name is then treated as a distinct object rather than resolving to the existing file. 

Note: This changes share behavior for clients that rely on case-insensitive name handling.

descriptions.value: An access control bypass flaw was identified in Samba's vfs_ceph_rgw module in it's openat() function. An authenticated user can bypass access controls to read or overwrite restricted files on shares configured with the experimental vfs_ceph_rgw module. When a client requests an existing file using mismatched character casing, the module fails to perform a case-insensitive lookup correctly, causing the server to treat the operation as creating a new file. As a result, the server skips standard permission checks on the existing file, allowing the attacker to access or overwrite sensitive data owned by other users.

cna.title: undici vulnerable to Subresource Integrity bypass via non-lowercase algorithm tokens

descriptions.value: undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions 7.15.0 through 7.30.0 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, its fetch() implementation verifies Subresource Integrity metadata by matching the algorithm token against a lowercase-only set, even though the SRI specification defines the token by its ASCII-lowercase form, so a valid but non-lowercase token such as an uppercase or mixed-case SHA256 is treated as unknown and skipped. When no recognized algorithm remains, undici treats the integrity list as empty and accepts the response, so a server returning a body that does not match the pinned digest passes the check. An attacker who controls only the response body can therefore deliver attacker-controlled bytes to an application that pinned a valid uppercase or mixed-case SRI token, with no integrity error, affecting response integrity only. The issue is fixed in undici 7.30.1 and 8.12.2, which normalize the algorithm token to ASCII lowercase before validation, and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As a workaround, use lowercase algorithm tokens such as sha256, sha384, or sha512 in integrity metadata.

cna.title: User Profile Builder <= 4.0.3 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation to 'role' Parameter via Legacy Meta-Name Collision on [wppb-register]

affected.product: User Profile Builder – Beautiful User Registration Forms, User Profiles & User Role Editor

descriptions.value: The User Profile Builder – Beautiful User Registration Forms, User Profiles & User Role Editor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Privilege Escalation in all versions up to, and including, 4.0.3 via the `role` parameter handled by the `wppb_add_meta_to_user_on_activation()` function. The vulnerability exists because the activation handler passes the attacker-supplied role value directly to `WP_User::set_role()` with no allow-list validation, and the 4.0.3 reserved-name check exempts pre-existing form fields from the block, allowing a legacy field with meta-name `role` to persist and bridge attacker-controlled request input into the serialized signup record stored in `wp_signups`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to gain a fully activated WordPress administrator account by submitting `role=administrator` through the public `[wppb-register]` shortcode form and subsequently clicking the confirmation activation link. Exploitation requires the site to have a legacy form field with meta-name `role` carried over from before the 4.0.3 upgrade, email confirmation enabled, and open user registration — all stable site-state conditions once established.

references.name: VulnCheck Advisory: Telegram-Stremio 5.1.0 Insecure Session Storage via encode_string

descriptions.value: Telegram-Stremio through 5.1.0 contains an insecure storage vulnerability that allows attackers with access to the MongoDB database, backups, or logs to recover the operator's authenticated Telegram session string, which is protected only by a keyless, reversible encoding transform rather than actual encryption. cna.title: WP STAGING <= 4.17.0 and WP STAGING Pro <= 6.17.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) PHP Object Injection to Remote Code Execution via Database Restore and Staging Reset

affected.product: WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups
WP STAGING Pro WordPress Backup Plugin

descriptions.value: The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

cna.title: psqlODBC SQLBindParameter heap memory corruption when binding more than 32767 parameters

descriptions.value: Integer wraparound in psqlODBC SQLBindParameter allows an application, or an attacker who controls how many parameters the application binds on one statement, to corrupt heap memory. psqlODBC stores the binding count in a signed 16-bit field. Binding parameter number 32768 wraps that count to -32768. Binding parameter 32769 then writes about 2.5 MB of zeros starting 1.25 MB before the binding array, which crashes the application or leaves it running on a corrupted heap. Applications that build parameter lists from untrusted input, such as an IN (?, ?, ...) list, are exposed. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0005 are affected.

workarounds.value: Do not bind more than 32767 parameters on a single statement. Limit the number of parameters an application builds from external input, or pass large value lists as a single array parameter, for example = ANY(?).

solutions.value: Upgrade to psqlODBC 18.00.0005 or later. SQLBindParameter now rejects parameter numbers outside 1..32767 with SQLSTATE 07009 (invalid descriptor index).

cna.x_redhatCweChain: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

descriptions.value: In HAProxy Data Plane API 2.2.0 through 3.4.3 (and corresponding Enterprise Edition releases), Server.ConfigureAPI() has process-global authentication logic that improperly drops security controls across multiple transport types. When a TLS Certificate Authority (tls_ca) is configured and a numeric TLS port (tls_port) is specified, the application globally disables Basic authentication on its shared internal request handler. Because this handler is shared concurrently among HTTP, HTTPS, and UNIX domain socket listeners, and mutual TLS (mTLS) client certificate verification (tls.RequireAndVerifyClientCert) is enforced exclusively on the HTTPS server path, all other simultaneously active non-mTLS listeners fail open. Consequently, an unauthenticated attacker capable of reaching an affected HTTP or UNIX management endpoint can completely bypass credentials to gain full API administrative access. This allows unauthorized remote or local actors to read sensitive, cleartext HAProxy configuration data or replace the managed configuration entirely via the raw configuration endpoint. This has been fixed in versions 3.4.4, 3.3.9, 3.2.17, 3.0.25, 2.9.29, and their respective EE backports by migrating to a per-request TLS connection-state validation model.

descriptions.value:
Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in the HTTP/2 implementation of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust server memory via a small HPACK-compressed HEADERS block. The block stores one large cookie value in the HPACK dynamic table and then references it tens of thousands of times with 1-byte indexed fields. In the reporter's run, a 49 KB block made a server with default settings allocate a 183 MB cookie binary before any application code ran, and every concurrent stream can repeat the cost.

Bandit.HTTP2.Connection caps only the compressed block (max_header_block_size), and its check of the decoded list against max_header_list_size never fires because that setting defaults to :infinity. combine_cookie_crumbs/1 in lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex then joins every crumb into one binary.

This issue affects bandit: from 0.3.3 before 1.14.0.

x_proofOfConcept.value:
* Against a Bandit server with default HTTP/2 settings, build an HPACK header block with the request pseudo-headers plus a 4,058-byte cookie stored in the dynamic table and then referenced about 45,000 times with indexed representations. The block is about 49 KB.
* Send it on one stream as a HEADERS frame followed by CONTINUATION frames of at most 16,384 bytes, with END_HEADERS on the last.
* The request reaches the plug with a cookie header of about 183 MB, and VM memory grows by about the same amount. Repeat on further streams to multiply it.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Compression

The attacker's header block, split across HEADERS and CONTINUATION frames, stays under the 50,000-byte max_header_block_size. It inserts one 4,058-byte cookie into the 4,096-byte dynamic table, the largest value that fits, then references it about 45,000 times with 1-byte indexed representations. HPAX.decode returns a list whose entries all point at the same binary, so decoding itself stays cheap.

2. Missing decoded limit (lib/bandit/http2/connection.ex, lib/bandit/http2/settings.ex)

After decoding, the connection compares header_list_size(headers) against local_settings.max_header_list_size. That setting defaults to :infinity, and in Erlang term order every integer sorts below an atom, so the comparison never rejects a list. The limit is enforced only when an operator sets it.

3. Expansion (lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex)

read_headers calls combine_cookie_crumbs/1, which joins every crumb with Enum.map_join/3 into a single binary of about 183 MB before Plug.call/2 runs. max_concurrent_streams also defaults to :infinity, so N streams allocate N times as much.

cna.title: netfilter: nf_flow_table: drop existing skb dst before skb_dst_set_noref()

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug fires in nf_flow_offload_ip_hook on NF_NETDEV_INGRESS when remotely sourced IPv4/IPv6 packets matching an offloaded flow are received on nftables flowtable-bound interfaces, not via netlink configuration APIs.
AC:L - Once a flowtable ingress hook and offloaded TCP/UDP flow exist, an attacker can reliably send matching traffic that reaches FLOW_OFFLOAD_XMIT_NEIGH or the XFRM offload path with a ref-counted skb dst; syzbot reproduced this without uncontrollable races.
PR:N - Exploitation requires only sending network traffic through an already deployed nftables flow-offload path on an ingress device; no local account, authentication, or CAP_NET_ADMIN on the victim is needed to trigger the leak.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required beyond normal network delivery; packets are processed automatically in softirq on the netdev ingress netfilter hook without opening files or mounting filesystems.
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel refcount imbalance and availability degradation on the affected host; this is standard in-kernel compromise territory, not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or other cross-authority scope change.
C:N - The flaw leaks a dst_entry reference by overwriting skb->_skb_refdst without releasing the prior dst; it does not expose kernel memory or provide an arbitrary read primitive.
I:N - No unauthorized data modification occurs; the skb is forwarded using the intended flowtable destination while the previous dst reference is orphaned, not corrupted into a controllable write primitive.
A:H - Each matching packet leaks a dst_entry refcount on the flowtable fast path, enabling sustained unauthenticated remote memory exhaustion on high-volume routers; CONFIG_DEBUG_NET builds also emit WARN_ON_ONCE during the overwrite.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: nf_flow_table: drop existing skb dst before skb_dst_set_noref()

Incoming skbs passing through netfilter flowtable offload hooks (or XFRM
offload path) might already carry a ref-counted dst_entry assigned during
earlier RX or routing steps.

Calling skb_dst_set_noref() when skb already holds a ref-counted dst
overwrites skb->_skb_refdst, leaking the previous dst_entry reference
count and triggering a DEBUG_NET_WARN_ON_ONCE assertion in
skb_dst_check_unset():

  WARNING: at skb_dst_check_unset include/linux/skbuff.h:1170
  WARNING: at skb_dst_set_noref include/linux/skbuff.h:1234
  WARNING: at nf_flow_offload_ip_hook+0xf6c/0x2b60 net/netfilter/nf_flow_table_ip.c:864

Drop any existing dst_entry reference with skb_dst_drop(skb) before
setting the non-referenced flowtable destination.

cna.title: ipv6: addrconf: bail out of dad_failure when state is no longer POSTDAD

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug is reached from inbound ICMPv6 Neighbor Discovery (NS/NA) packets processed by icmp6_rcv()→ndisc_rcv()→addrconf_dad_failure(), the standard IPv6 network receive path on internet-facing servers, cloud VMs, phones, and IoT devices on shared L2 segments.
AC:L - An attacker controls both sides of the race by flooding forged NS/NA during DAD while concurrently triggering ipv6_del_addr() via RTM_DELADDR/CAP_NET_ADMIN in a user namespace, CNI/orchestration address teardown, or interface-down processing; retries make the narrow window reliably winnable.
PR:N - Triggering DAD failure requires only unauthenticated ND packet injection on the victim's link; the concurrent ipv6_del_addr() leg needs no victim credentials and can come from automatic address lifecycle events (CNI churn, SLAAC/privacy regeneration, netdev down) rather than attacker admin rights.
UI:N - Exploitation does not require any victim user action such as opening files or mounting filesystems; it targets automatic IPv6 address configuration and DAD processing that occurs during normal network connectivity and boot.
S:U - The corrupted inet6_ifaddr lifecycle and resulting kernel crash occur within kernel memory management; impact does not cross a VM, container, or IOMMU security boundary into a separate authority.
C:H - The race leaves a freed/partially torn-down inet6_ifaddr with corrupted state and a poisoned RCU list entry (LIST_POISON2), constituting use-after-free class memory corruption that can expose adjacent kernel heap contents beyond a pure crash.
I:H - Corrupting inet6_ifaddr state after list_del_rcu() and re-queuing dad_work on a dead object enables heap reuse and control of freed object contents, providing a path to arbitrary kernel memory writes and potential code execution beyond denial of service.
A:H - The demonstrated failure is a general protection fault in ipv6_del_addr() from addrconf_dad_work on the ipv6_addrconf workqueue, causing a kernel oops/panic and complete loss of system availability on affected hosts.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: addrconf: bail out of dad_failure when state is no longer POSTDAD

addrconf_dad_failure() transitions ifp->state from DAD to POSTDAD
via addrconf_dad_end(), which drops ifp->lock on return.  The lock
is re-acquired after net_info_ratelimited().  A concurrent
ipv6_del_addr() can take the lock in that window, set ifp->state
to DEAD and run list_del_rcu(&ifp->if_list).

addrconf_dad_failure() then overwrites DEAD with ERRDAD at errdad:
and schedules a new dad_work.  The work calls ipv6_del_addr()
again, hitting the already-poisoned list entry:

  general protection fault: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 4 PID: 217 Comm: kworker/4:1
  Workqueue: ipv6_addrconf addrconf_dad_work
  RIP: 0010:ipv6_del_addr+0xe9/0x280
  RAX: dead000000000122
  Call Trace:
   addrconf_dad_stop+0x113/0x140
   addrconf_dad_work+0x28c/0x430
   process_one_work+0x1eb/0x3b0
   worker_thread+0x4d/0x400
   kthread+0x104/0x140
   ret_from_fork+0x35/0x40

Fold the addrconf_dad_end() logic into addrconf_dad_failure() under
a single ifp->lock critical section.  The STABLE_PRIVACY branch
temporarily drops ifp->lock around address regeneration, so at
lock_errdad: verify the state is still POSTDAD before transitioning
to ERRDAD; bail out otherwise to avoid overwriting a state set by
another path while the lock was released.

cna.title: mm/huge_memory: fix huge_zero_pfn race

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Reached only through local page faults in handle_mm_fault()->create_huge_pmd()->do_huge_pmd_anonymous_page()->mm_get_huge_zero_folio() racing shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan(); no network, adjacent, or physical path exists.
AC:L - Attacker controls both race sides: concurrent anonymous read faults drive get_huge_zero_folio() while memory-pressure reclaim drives shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan(); multi-threaded hammering makes the preemption window reliably winnable.
PR:L - Any unprivileged local process can mmap anonymous memory and trigger huge-zero PMD installation on typical CONFIG_TRANSPARENT_HUGEPAGE systems with zero-page enabled; no root, capabilities, or authentication is required.
UI:N - Exploitation is fully attacker-driven via standard syscalls (mmap, madvise, read, munmap) and deliberate memory pressure; no separate victim action beyond the attacker running their own workload is needed.
S:U - Corrupts kernel-global huge_zero_folio metadata and rmap/RSS accounting within the kernel security boundary; this is not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or cross-authority sandbox break.
C:H - Misidentification routes the shared huge zero folio through normal THP split/teardown (folio_remove_rmap_pmd, incorrect accounting), corrupting global page metadata with plausible arbitrary kernel memory disclosure leverage.
I:H - Wrong-path splitting manipulates refcount/rmap state on the system-wide huge zero singleton folio, corrupting kernel integrity and enabling memory-write/control-flow primitives from metadata corruption.
A:H - Mis-split triggers kernel WARN/BUG_ON, bad page state, and bad rss-counter failures during reclaim or teardown, causing kernel oops, panic, or hang on affected THP systems.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mm/huge_memory: fix huge_zero_pfn race

Patch series "mm/huge_memory: fix huge_zero_pfn race", v2.

There is a subtle race in the reference-counted huge_zero_folio
implementation.

The fast path atomic logic fails to account for the fact that the shrinker
(which drops the final huge_zero_refcount pin) can overwrite huge_zero_pfn
with the ~0UL sentinel value in shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan() after a
racing get_huge_zero_folio() installed a valid value there.

This results in huge_zero_folio being correctly set but huge_zero_pfn
being set incorrectly and thus is_huge_zero_pfn() and consequently
is_huge_zero_pmd() will misidentify the huge zero folio as being an
ordinary THP folio.

This can result in the huge zero folio being split and otherwise treated
incorrectly.

The solution to this is very subtle as there is an atomic fast path, and
thus ordering in weakly ordered architectures has to be treated very
carefully.

The first commit fixes the issue by introducing a spinlock around
huge_zero_[pfn, folio, refcount] write, with careful consideration paid to
load/store ordering in the fast path.  It is placed first and kept as
small as possible so that it can be backported on its own.

The second commit is a pure cleanup which reworks the
CONFIG_PERSISTENT_HUGE_ZERO_FOLIO logic to better separate the persistent
logic from the dynamically allocated one.


This patch (of 2):

If !CONFIG_PERSISTENT_HUGE_ZERO_FOLIO, the huge_zero_folio is refcounted
by huge_zero_refcount and returned by mm_get_huge_zero_folio().

When the caller is done with the huge zero page, its reference count is
decremented.  Only a shrinker can set the reference count to zero.

A race can unfortunately occur between a shrinker decrementing the
reference count to zero and a concurrent page fault.

This is because shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan() might, if very unlucky, be
preempted between setting huge_zero_refcount to zero and writing an
invalid value.

During this time get_huge_zero_folio() could write to huge_zero_pfn before
shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan() resumes.

In this event the huge zero folio will be persistently misidentified
causing the THP code path to be entered inappropriately for the huge zero
folio:

                CPU 0                                   CPU 1
=======================================|=================================
shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan()          |
   atomic_cmpxchg() sets refcount to 0 |
   xchg() sets huge_zero_folio to NULL | get_huge_zero_folio()
                 |                     |    atomic_inc_not_zero() -> zero
      preempted for a long time        |    Allocate new huge zero folio
                 |                     |    Write valid huge_zero_folio
                 v                     |    Write valid huge_zero_pfn
  Overwrite huge_zero_pfn with ~0UL   <--- Invalid overwrite!

This results in is_huge_zero_pfn() and is_huge_zero_pmd() incorrectly
returning false for a huge zero page which could result in issues like the
huge zero folio being incorrectly split.

Note that the issue is with huge_zero_pfn not huge_zero_folio, as
get_huge_zero_folio() uses cmpxchg() gated on huge_zero_folio being NULL
with a retry loop and shrink_huge_zero_folio_scan() uses xchg() to set
huge_zero_folio.

Fix the issue by introducing a spinlock, huge_zero_lock, to prevent
concurrent write of huge_zero_folio, huge_zero_pfn and huge_zero_refcount.

There needs to be significant care taken here to ensure correctness:

The fast path in get_huge_zero_folio() uses atomic_inc_not_zero(), which
is outside of the critical section, and means huge zero allocation is
gated on zero huge_zero_refcount.

The fast path doesn't use huge_zero_lock, so the critical section is
irrelevant to it.

So invariants are required - huge_zero_refcount MUST:

* Only be set in the huge_zero_lock critical section to ensure
  serialisation of huge_zero_pfn, huge_zero_folio and
---truncated---

cna.title: ocfs2/dlm: require a ref for locking_state debugfs open

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ocfs2/dlm: require a ref for locking_state debugfs open

debug_lockres_open() copies inode->i_private into struct debug_lockres and
debug_lockres_release() later drops that pointer with dlm_put().  That
only works if open successfully pins the struct dlm_ctxt.

Today open calls dlm_grab(dlm) but ignores its return value.  Once the
last domain unregister has removed the context from dlm_domains,
dlm_grab() returns NULL, yet open still stores the raw pointer and returns
success.  The later release path is outside the debugfs removal barrier,
so it can call dlm_put() after dlm_free_ctxt_mem() has freed the context. 
KASAN reports this as a slab-use-after-free in dlm_put() called from
debug_lockres_release().

Fail the open when dlm_grab() cannot acquire the reference and unwind the
seq_file private state before returning.  That keeps locking_state from
handing out a file descriptor whose release path does not own the
dlm_ctxt.

The buggy scenario involves two paths, with each column showing the order
within that path:

locking_state debugfs open:          last domain unregister:
1. debug_lockres_open() reads        1. dlm_unregister_domain() calls
   inode->i_private.                    dlm_complete_dlm_shutdown().
2. debug_lockres_open() calls        2. shutdown removes the dlm_ctxt from
   dlm_grab(dlm) and gets NULL.         dlm_domains.
3. open still stores the raw dlm     3. final teardown reaches
   pointer in dl->dl_ctxt and           dlm_free_ctxt_mem() and frees it.
   returns success.
4. debug_lockres_release() later

cna.title: veth: convert frag_list skbs before running XDP

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug is hit when a received skb traverses veth XDP processing; in cloud/container deployments (e.g. Cloudflare-style edge nodes) remote traffic routed to a veth peer with XDP+AF_XDP can deliver the malformed frag_list skb without local access.
AC:L - An attacker can reliably supply the required frag_list skb (data_len>0, nr_frags=0) by transmitting from the veth peer via sockets or GRO aggregation, controlling packet size, timing, and content without depending on uncontrollable kernel state.
PR:N - Remote exploitation needs no attacker privileges when ingress traffic reaches a veth that already has an XDP program redirecting to an AF_XDP socket; only network-delivered skbs trigger veth_convert_skb_to_xdp_buff() and the faulty __xsk_rcv() path.
UI:N - No victim user action is required beyond normal network traffic reaching the veth interface; exploitation is automatic once a qualifying frag_list skb is received and redirected to AF_XDP copy mode.
S:U - The flaw causes kernel memory reads and crashes within the host kernel security boundary; it does not cross VM, hypervisor, or IOMMU isolation boundaries.
C:H - Bogus XDP_FLAGS_HAS_FRAGS metadata makes __xsk_rcv() memcpy from uninitialized frags[] entries via skb_frag_address(), enabling out-of-bounds kernel memory reads into the AF_XDP receive buffer before faulting.
I:N - The failure mode is a kernel-side memcpy read using invalid fragment metadata; data is copied into the attacker's AF_XDP ring buffer rather than corrupting kernel or other tenants' memory for integrity purposes.
A:H - The commit and code path confirm a kernel crash when __xsk_rcv() follows bogus fragment metadata and memcpy faults on an invalid frags[] source address, causing oops/panic and denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

veth: convert frag_list skbs before running XDP

A frag_list skb can reach veth with data_len set but nr_frags zero.
veth_convert_skb_to_xdp_buff() only converts skbs that are shared,
locked, have frags[], or do not have enough headroom. It later uses
skb_is_nonlinear() to decide whether to set XDP_FLAGS_HAS_FRAGS and
xdp_frags_size.

That exposes frag_list data to XDP as if it were stored in frags[], but
frags[] is empty. AF_XDP copy mode can then trust the bogus XDP fragment
metadata, walk an empty fragment entry, and crash in memcpy() from
__xsk_rcv().

Route non-linear skbs through skb_pp_cow_data() before exposing them to
XDP, and only advertise XDP frags when the resulting skb has frags[].
skb_copy_bits() already handles frag_list input, and skb_pp_cow_data()
builds frags[] output with skb_add_rx_frag(), which is the
representation XDP multi-buffer expects.

cna.title: binfmt_misc: use exe_file_deny_write_access() for the interpreter clone

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

binfmt_misc: use exe_file_deny_write_access() for the interpreter clone

For MISC_FMT_OPEN_FILE entries load_misc_binary() clones the
registered interpreter file and denies write access to the clone via
plain deny_write_access(). The clone is installed as
bprm->interpreter and later released by the exec machinery through
exe_file_allow_write_access() which skips the i_writecount increment
for files with FMODE_FSNOTIFY_HSM set.

The deny and allow side can therefore come to different conclusions
when pre-content watches are in play: if a pre-content watch is added
to the interpreter after registration every subsequent exec through
that entry takes a write denial on the clone that is never paired
with a write allowance, driving the interpreter inode's i_writecount
further down with each exec and leaving the interpreter unwritable
even after the entry and all its users are gone.

Take the write denial via exe_file_deny_write_access() so both sides
of the pairing base their decision on the same file mode, and
propagate failure instead of silently ignoring it: an interpreter
that is concurrently open for writing now fails the exec with
ETXTBSY, exactly like an interpreter freshly opened via open_exec()
would.

cna.title: packet: synchronize pressure clearing with ring reconfiguration

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The bug is hit only from local AF_PACKET syscalls—setsockopt(PACKET_RX_RING) racing poll(2)/recvmsg(2) pressure clearing in packet_poll()/packet_recvmsg()—not from remote packet receive paths like ksmbd, nfsd, or the TCP/IP stack.
AC:L - The attacker controls both race sides: one thread polls/recvmsg while PACKET_SOCK_PRESSURE is set, another tears down the RX ring via PACKET_RX_RING; packet_set_ring()'s synchronize_net() window makes the stale tpacket_rcv vs NULL/freed pg_vec mismatch reliably winnable.
PR:L - packet_create() requires ns_capable(net->user_ns, CAP_NET_RAW); unprivileged users obtain CAP_NET_RAW via user+network namespaces (unshare -Urn) or container defaults (Docker NET_RAW), without init-namespace root.
UI:N - No victim action is required; the attacker creates the AF_PACKET socket, configures the mmap RX ring, fills it to set PACKET_SOCK_PRESSURE, and races ring teardown against its own poll/recvmsg calls.
S:U - Stale/NULL ring dereferences corrupt kernel heap state on the same host; this is standard kernel memory corruption within one security authority, not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or other cross-boundary scope change.
C:H - __packet_rcv_has_room() follows tpacket_rcv and dereferences rb->pg_vec or prb_bdqc block pointers after packet_set_ring() cleared/freed the ring, yielding NULL-dereference or use-after-free reads of ring metadata and mmap-backed pages.
I:H - Freed ring storage and stale prb_bdqc/pkbdq pointers remain attacker-influenced through mmap and concurrent ring operations, providing a controllable kernel heap use-after-free write primitive typical of AF_PACKET ring reconfiguration races.
A:H - NULL pg_vec indexing in packet_lookup_frame() or stale block access in prb_lookup_block() from the pressure-clearing path causes an immediate kernel oops/panic, giving any qualifying local attacker repeatable host-wide denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

packet: synchronize pressure clearing with ring reconfiguration

packet_set_ring() updates the RX ring state under sk_receive_queue.lock,
but used to publish the tpacket receive mode through po->prot_hook.func
after releasing that lock. packet_poll() and packet_recvmsg() can then
run the pressure clearing path after the ring has been cleared while
still seeing tpacket_rcv, causing __packet_rcv_has_room() to dereference
stale or NULL ring storage.

Move the existing receive hook assignment into the same
sk_receive_queue.lock section as the ring state update. Keep the
assignment otherwise unchanged, including on TX ring reconfiguration, to
avoid adding behavior changes that are not required for the fix.

Serialize packet_recvmsg() pressure clearing with the same queue lock
only after PACKET_SOCK_PRESSURE has been observed. If the flag is clear
and the socket has moved away from tpacket_rcv, packet_set_ring() has
already detached the socket and waited for synchronize_net(), so no new
packet input can set the flag again.

packet_poll() already holds sk_receive_queue.lock, so it uses the new
unlocked helper directly.

cna.title: fscrypt: use the mount idmap for the owner check in fscrypt_ioctl_set_policy()

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Exploitation requires a local process to open a directory on an idmapped ext4/f2fs filesystem and issue FS_IOC_SET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY via ioctl(); there is no network, adjacent-radio, or physical-device attack path to the vulnerable fscrypt_ioctl_set_policy() check.
AC:L - On idmapped mounts the UID mismatch is structural, not random: any local user whose fsuid equals the inode's unmapped on-disk owner can open an empty victim directory, add their own fscrypt key, and trigger the ioctl without races or attacker-uncontrollable memory layout.
PR:L - Only basic local user privileges are needed; the attacker must be able to open the target directory and call FS_IOC_ADD_ENCRYPTION_KEY plus FS_IOC_SET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY, with no real-root or init-namespace capability required beyond normal DAC permissions on the path.
UI:N - Exploitation requires no action by the victim; the attacker alone issues the ioctl on an empty directory they can open, and the authorization bypass occurs entirely within the attacker's own syscall sequence.
S:U - This is an incorrect inode_owner_or_capable() authorization check in the kernel fscrypt ioctl path on idmapped mounts; impact stays within the same kernel security authority and does not constitute VM escape, hypervisor bypass, or IOMMU boundary crossing.
C:H - A wrongly authorized attacker can bind a victim's empty directory to an attacker-controlled fscrypt master key, then decrypt any sensitive files the victim later creates there, giving broad read access to victim data rather than a small bounded leak.
I:H - The ioctl persistently modifies filesystem encryption policy and on-disk fscrypt context for a directory the attacker does not own, granting unauthorized control over a critical security property of victim data at rest.
A:H - The bug both wrongly denies legitimate directory owners with -EACCES and lets attackers encrypt a victim's empty directory with an attacker-held key, preventing the real owner from using or recovering that directory and its future contents.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

fscrypt: use the mount idmap for the owner check in fscrypt_ioctl_set_policy()

fscrypt_ioctl_set_policy() calls inode_owner_or_capable() with
&nop_mnt_idmap before allowing an encryption policy to be set, instead
of the idmap of the mount the ioctl was issued on.

fscrypt is used by filesystems that support idmapped mounts (e.g. ext4,
f2fs), so on such a mount this compares the caller's fsuid against the
unmapped on-disk owner rather than the mapped owner: the actual owner
can be wrongly denied with -EACCES and an unrelated caller wrongly
allowed.  Use file_mnt_idmap(filp) instead.

cna.title: bnxt: fix head underflow on XDP head-grow

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The flaw is reached in bnxt hardware RX/NAPI processing when network packets arrive; the reproducing selftest triggers it by exchanging UDP packets over the network after XDP head-grow on receive.
AC:L - Once a bnxt interface runs XDP multi-buffer with jumbo MTU, an attacker can reliably trigger bpf_xdp_adjust_head(-256) with packets larger than rx_copybreak (256 bytes); no race or attacker-uncontrollable memory layout is required.
PR:N - The vulnerable receive path performs no authentication on incoming packets. Attaching the XDP program and enabling jumbo MTU are deployment preconditions on affected bnxt servers, not privileges the remote attacker needs.
UI:N - After the affected bnxt interface is configured with XDP and jumbo MTU, exploitation requires only sending crafted network traffic; no additional victim action such as opening files or mounting filesystems is needed.
S:U - Impact is kernel memory corruption and denial of service within the host networking stack. This is standard in-kernel privilege/integrity impact, not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or other cross-security-boundary violation.
C:H - Pointer underflow builds the skb on the wrong page-pool fragment or prior physical page, corrupting refcount accounting and allowing pages to be recycled while still referenced, yielding a use-after-free that can expose kernel memory.
I:H - Corrupted page-pool reference counts can prematurely recycle receive buffers still in use and lead to double-free on teardown, providing exploitable kernel heap memory corruption beyond a simple crash.
A:H - The bug crashes bnxt systems during XDP head-grow testing and can be triggered repeatedly via received traffic, causing kernel oops, resource exhaustion, or panic especially when panic_on_warn is enabled.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bnxt: fix head underflow on XDP head-grow

The xdp.py test test_xdp_native_adjst_head_grow_data crashes when run on
a bnxt machine (and also crashes in NIPA).

It seems that the bug is an underflow in bnxt_rx_multi_page_skb, which
builds the skb head:

  napi_build_skb(data_ptr - bp->rx_offset, rxr->rx_page_size);

The problem with this expression is that in page mode, rx_offset is:

  bp->rx_offset = NET_IP_ALIGN + XDP_PACKET_HEADROOM;

Which evaluates (at least on x86_64) to 258.

The test test_xdp_native_adjst_head_grow_data tests a case where the
head is adjusted by -256.

When this test runs, data_ptr is shifted to frag_start + 2 (where
frag_start = page_address(page) + offset).

Then, bnxt_rx_multi_page_skb is invoked and the napi_build_skb
expression subtracts 258, landing at an address before frag_start. This
could be either the previous fragment or the previous physical page when
the offset is < 256 (e.g. if the fragment started at offset 0).

When the skb is freed, the page pool fragment reference is dropped on
either the wrong page or the wrong frag of the right page. In either
case, the corrupted reference count can lead to the page being
prematurely recycled while still in use. Once (incorrectly) recycled, it
can be handed out again and on driver teardown this would result in a
double free.

The commit under fixes updated this code to handle the case where the
native page size is >= 64k, but it unintentionally broke the head grow
case.

To fix this, add an offset field to struct bnxt_sw_rx_bd, mirroring the
existing offset field in struct bnxt_sw_rx_agg_bd. Populate it on
allocation and preserve it on reuse.

In bnxt_rx_multi_page_skb, use the newly added offset field to compute
the fragment start and pass that to napi_build_skb. Adjust the layout
with skb_reserve.

There are two cases, the non-adjustment case and the adjustment case.

In both cases, the skb is built at page_address(page) + offset to
account for the case where the native page size >= 64K and skb_reserve
is called with data_ptr - (page_address(page) + offset). That
difference equals bp->rx_offset when data_ptr was not moved, or
bp->rx_offset + xdp_adjust when XDP adjusted the head.

Re-running the failing test with this commit applied causes the test to
run successfully to completion.

The other rx_skb_func implementations don't have this issue.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Net-IDN-Encode 2.590-TRIAL or later.

descriptions.value:
Net::IDN::Punycode versions before 2.590 for Perl allow an out-of-bounds read via integer overflow of the delta accumulator in encode_punycode.

The XS backend keeps the punycode delta, and the digit index derived from it, in a signed int. The accumulation `delta += (m-n) * (h+1)` has no overflow check, so a large enough code point wraps the delta and the digit index leaves the range of the 36-entry digit table. The bound before the final table access tests only for an index above 36, so a negative index passes it, as does 36 itself. Perl strings hold code points beyond the Unicode range, and one such code point overflows the accumulation on its own. Valid input wraps it as well, for example 1927 ASCII letters followed by U+10FFFF. The conversion functions encode a label before they check its length, so a long label reaches the encoder through the documented API.

Only the XS backend is affected.

Encoding an attacker-supplied string copies a byte from outside the digit table into the encoded result or crashes the process.

cna.title: audit: fix potential use-after-free in audit_del_rule()

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Reachable only via local NETLINK_AUDIT (AUDIT_DEL_RULE) or filesystem events that autoremove AUDIT_EXE rules; concurrent UAF readers run in syscall/io_uring exit audit filtering on the local host, not from remote network input.
AC:L - The attacker controls both sides of the race by deleting an AUDIT_EXE rule (auditctl or deleting/moving the audited executable) while driving concurrent syscall/io_uring activity to keep RCU readers in audit_filter()/audit_filter_rules().
PR:L - Besides CAP_AUDIT_CONTROL netlink deletion, unprivileged local users can trigger audit_del_rule() via fsnotify autoremove when deleting/moving an admin-configured audited executable they can write, without init-namespace root.
UI:N - Exploitation requires no victim interaction; the attacker schedules rule deletion and concurrent audited syscalls/io_uring exits to hit the UAF window.
S:U - Impact is kernel heap memory corruption and local privilege escalation within the host kernel security domain, not a documented cross-VM or IOMMU boundary escape.
C:H - Use-after-free of audit_fsnotify_mark while audit_exe_compare()/audit_mark_compare() dereference mark->ino/dev enables arbitrary kernel memory reads and info disclosure primitives.
I:H - Freed fsnotify mark objects can be reallocated and corrupted to obtain arbitrary kernel writes, control-flow hijack, and local root code execution beyond audit rule deletion.
A:H - Concurrent dereference of a freed audit_fsnotify_mark during audit filtering can immediately oops/panic the kernel; repeated triggering yields reliable denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

audit: fix potential use-after-free in audit_del_rule()

`audit_del_rule()` destroys `e->rule.exe` via `audit_remove_mark_rule()`
before unlinking the rule from RCU-visible filter lists and waiting for a
grace period. Concurrent readers in `audit_filter()` and
`audit_filter_rules()` still dereference `e->rule.exe`, while the fsnotify
mark can be freed on an independent lifetime path. This creates a
use-after-free window during rule deletion.

Fix this by unlinking the rule from the RCU-visible lists and invoking
`synchronize_rcu()` before calling `audit_remove_mark_rule()` (and other
rule removal helpers). This ensures that all existing RCU readers have
exited the critical section before any underlying resources are destroyed.

cna.title: nvme: fix FDP fdpcidx bounds check

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug is in the NVMe host driver while parsing Get Features/Get Log responses during namespace scan; a malicious NVMe-oF target can deliver crafted FDP data over TCP/RDMA to any host already using remote NVMe storage, which is the highest-impact reachable deployment.
AC:L - An attacker controlling the NVMe endpoint fully sets fdpcidx and numfdpc in protocol responses and can reliably make fdpcidx equal numfdpc+1, walk one descriptor past the valid list, and hit the out-of-bounds read without races or victim-specific heap layout.
PR:N - Exploitation needs no local account or capabilities on the victim; a remote malicious/compromised NVMe-oF target (or physical device inserted by an attacker) triggers parsing during connect/rescan/AEN-driven namespace scans without further local authorization.
UI:N - No victim user action is required at exploit time because namespace scanning and AEN-triggered rescans run automatically in kernel workqueues once a controller is present, and a remote target can force rescans with Notice Namespace Changed events.
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel memory and block-layer metadata on the host parsing the malicious device responses; it does not cross a VM, container, or IOMMU security boundary into a separate authority.
C:H - Accepting fdpcidx=numfdpc+1 lets the descriptor walk advance past the last valid FDP configuration and then reads desc->nrg and desc->runs out of bounds, leaking adjacent kvmalloc/heap contents or attacker-crafted bytes from beyond the valid descriptor array.
I:H - The out-of-bounds descriptor fields are copied into info->runs and influence queue write_stream_granularity limits, giving attacker-controlled modification of kernel block-layer state from memory corruption primitives that can be chained beyond a simple crash.
A:H - If the out-of-bounds descriptor pointer lies past the allocated FDP log buffer, accessing desc->nrg/desc->runs can fault the kernel (oops/panic); even successful parsing still represents unsafe memory access with high availability risk under attacker control.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nvme: fix FDP fdpcidx bounds check

The fdpcidx bounds check sets n = NUMFDPC + 1 but used > instead of >=,
incorrectly accepting fdp_idx when it equals n (i.e. NUMFDPC + 1).

cna.title: bpf: Preserve pointer state for commuted arithmetic

scenarios.value:
AV:L - The flaw is in bpf_check()/adjust_ptr_min_max_vals() during bpf(BPF_PROG_LOAD) via the local bpf(2) syscall; per kernel CNA guidance BPF verifier bugs are Local, not reachable from remote network packet handling.
AC:L - An attacker fully controls BPF bytecode using commuted 64-bit scalar+=pointer ALU and bpf2bpf call chains, deterministically poisoning register state during verification without races or external preconditions.
PR:L - Exploitation requires loading bpf2bpf programs (CAP_BPF-gated), which is routinely available to unprivileged users via user namespaces/BPF token delegation or unprivileged socket-filter loading when kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=0, not init-namespace root.
UI:N - The attacker loads and executes their own crafted BPF program through bpf(2); no separate victim action such as mounting filesystems or opening files is required beyond the attacker's own local access.
S:U - Impact is a BPF verifier bypass enabling in-kernel out-of-bounds memory access and privilege escalation within the host kernel's security authority; it does not cross VM, IOMMU, or sandbox boundaries.
C:H - Copying only type/id on scalar+=pointer leaves stale frameno, var_off, and map/parent metadata, so bpf_func() stack checks validate the wrong frame and approve out-of-bounds reads of adjacent kernel memory.
I:H - The same incorrect pointer provenance permits verifier-approved out-of-bounds BPF stack/map writes at runtime, a controllable kernel memory corruption primitive leverageable for arbitrary modification and privilege escalation.
A:H - Out-of-bounds BPF memory accesses from the bypassed verifier state can corrupt critical kernel data or dereference invalid addresses, reliably causing kernel oops/panic and repeatable denial of service.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bpf: Preserve pointer state for commuted arithmetic

When scalar += pointer is handled in adjust_ptr_min_max_vals(), the
destination register inherits the pointer state from the source pointer.
Copying only selected fields is fragile because pointer provenance is
tracked by several bpf_reg_state fields.

Use the caller's temporary offset register to preserve the scalar operand
while replacing the destination with the full pointer state. This preserves
the frame number for PTR_TO_STACK registers and keeps parent identity
fields consistent.

cna.title: net: openvswitch: fix skb leak on flow key update failure during ct

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: openvswitch: fix skb leak on flow key update failure during ct

ovs_ct_execute() always steals or frees the skb on failure while
ovs_flow_key_update() does not.  So, if it fails and we return right
away, the skb ends up leaked.

Fix that by breaking instead and letting the common error handling
code at the bottom of the loop to free the skb properly.

This is a very unlikely scenario as it requires the packet to become
unparseable by applying a set of actions on a previously parseable skb,
but should be fixed nevertheless.

Reported by Sashiko.

cna.title: net/sched: act_ct: fix sk_buff leak when the header checks reject a packet

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The leak is triggered in tcf_ct_act() on the packet datapath (netif_receive_skb → sch_handle_ingress/egress → tc_run → tcf_classify); on OVN/Kubernetes/SDN gateways and mlx5-offload nodes with act_ct on clsact, a remote peer sends malformed IP packets with no local access required.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls packet contents; a 54-byte IPv6 frame with nexthdr=0 (hop-by-hop) and no trailing data deterministically makes ipv6_find_hdr() return -EPROTO, leaking one skb per packet without races or uncontrollable layout dependencies.
PR:N - Installing act_ct requires CAP_NET_ADMIN, but triggering the leak on an already-configured internet-facing or tenant-facing gateway needs no target credentials; a remote attacker only sends crafted malformed IP packets, matching CNA precedent for packet-driven act_ct issues (e.g., CVE-2026-72057).
UI:N - Exploitation requires only attacker-generated malformed packets reaching a host with act_ct on clsact/ingress or egress; no victim login, mount, or other interactive action is needed beyond normal network traffic processing.
S:U - The leaked sk_buff objects remain within the host kernel memory domain; this is not a VM escape, sandbox breakout, or IOMMU boundary bypass, only unbounded kernel heap consumption on the affected node.
C:N - This is a pure sk_buff ownership leak on an error path; skb memory is orphaned, not exposed to the attacker, with no out-of-bounds read, use-after-free, or other disclosure primitive.
I:N - The flaw only fails to kfree_skb() when header validation rejects a packet; it does not corrupt, overwrite, or modify any memory contents and provides no write or code-execution primitive.
A:H - Each malformed packet leaks one sk_buff plus its data buffer (~936 bytes); sustained remote flooding causes unbounded kernel memory exhaustion and OOM denial of service, matching CNA precedent for repeatable network-triggered skb leaks (e.g., CVE-2026-52974).
