descriptions.value:
Kunai, a security monitoring tool, contains a time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition in its mount namespace (mnt ns) caching logic. When resolving a security event that references a specific process PID and an expected mount namespace, the Switcher::new function read /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt to determine the target namespace and cached the result under the expected namespace key without verifying that the resolved namespace actually matched the expected one.

An attacker with local access could exploit this by either (1) arranging for the referenced PID to be reused by a process in a different namespace (e.g., the host namespace) before Kunai resolves it, or (2) calling unshare or setns on the target process after the event is generated but before the namespace is resolved. In either case, the wrong namespace (potentially the host's own namespace) would be cached under the container's namespace key.

The security impact is that subsequent container security events would be resolved against host filesystem paths rather than container paths. This undermines the integrity of the security monitoring data: container activity could be misattributed to the host, host activity could be misattributed to a container, and file-path-based detections or alerts would reference incorrect paths. An attacker could potentially use this to obscure malicious activity within a container by making it appear as benign host activity, or to generate misleading security alerts.

The vulnerability requires local access to the system and a specific timing window between event generation and namespace resolution. No remote attack vector or user interaction is required.

cna.title: PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction

descriptions.value: CAPEC-129 Pointer Manipulation

PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction.

The PHP CGI binary (php-cgi), in CGI and FastCGI mode with cgi.fix_pathinfo enabled (the default), can perform an out-of-bounds read and write when the path removed from SCRIPT_FILENAME or PATH_TRANSLATED is longer than the supplied PATH_INFO, or when PATH_INFO is empty. This requires a web server mapping that passes such inconsistent values, or a FastCGI listener reachable by untrusted clients. An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the process, may obtain process memory if the application exposes PATH_INFO or PATH_TRANSLATED, and may corrupt memory. PHP-FPM and the Apache module are not affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: Guard Core: Whitespace-collapse preprocessing permanently disables the CRLF-anchored http-splitting and command-injection detectors in the default detection mode

descriptions.value: Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, ContentPreprocessor.preprocess() in guard_core/detection_engine/preprocessor.py collapses all whitespace before built-in pattern matching in the default enhanced mode. This removes carriage returns and newlines required by the http_split and newline-anchored cmd_injection detectors in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py, making those detectors unable to match. Framework-decoded CRLF can therefore pass through Guard Core unflagged while the downstream application still receives the raw newline-bearing value. Direct security impact requires a downstream stack or application that persists or re-emits the value into a CRLF-tolerant response or command context. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

cna.title: Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider: S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator disables S3 TLS verification by default

descriptions.value: In the Apache Airflow Microsoft Azure provider 10.2.0 through 15.3.0, `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` turned off TLS certificate verification for its connection to Amazon S3 by default (`s3_verify=False`), whatever the AWS connection's own verification settings were. Deployments are affected when a Dag uses `S3ToAzureBlobStorageOperator` without setting `s3_verify`. Users are advised to upgrade to apache-airflow-providers-microsoft-azure 15.3.1 or later, which uses the AWS connection's verification settings by default.

cna.title: Kubeshark: MCP `start_kubeshark` argument injection via `pod_regex` → image redirect → cluster takeover

descriptions.value: Kubeshark is an eBPF-powered network observability tool for Kubernetes. From 53.1.0 until 53.4.0, the start_kubeshark MCP tool in cmd/mcpRunner.go uses callStartKubeshark to append caller-controlled pod_regex as a bare positional argument to kubeshark tap without a -- end-of-options separator, allowing a value beginning with --set to be parsed as a Helm value override. An attacker who influences tool arguments against kubeshark mcp --allow-destructive can redirect the privileged worker, Hub, and front images through tap.docker.registry and tap.docker.tag to an attacker-controlled registry. cna.title: JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending a one-byte chunk in incr_parse

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending a one-byte chunk in incr_parse.

The incremental buffer grows to one and a half times the length it must hold, with no room reserved for the terminating NUL. For an empty buffer and a one-byte chunk that request is one byte, which a buffer whose front was removed by earlier decodes can already have, so nothing is reallocated and the NUL lands one byte past the allocation.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer, choosing how the input is split into reads, can cause a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write.

descriptions.value: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. cna.title: PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation

descriptions.value: CAPEC-69 Target Programs with Elevated Privileges

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source

solutions.value: Upgrade to a future IO-Socket-SSL release, or apply the upstream patch.

workarounds.value: Until a fixed release is available, do not run update_self_from_url.

descriptions.value:
IO::Socket::SSL::PublicSuffix versions through 2.099 for Perl allow code injection via a fetched list line that closes the built-in data heredoc when update_self_from_url rewrites the module's source.

The rewrite copies the module's source down to the built-in list's heredoc and appends each fetched line below it. Nothing checks that a line looks like a domain. A line that is not a comment loses only what follows a `//` and its trailing whitespace, so a line reading END_BUILTIN_DATA is appended as it stands and ends the data block in the rewritten file. Every fetched line after it is Perl.

Arbitrary Perl runs in every process that loads IO::Socket::SSL, which loads this module unconditionally, until the file is reinstalled. The attacker must control the fetched list, through the cleartext default URL or a caller-supplied one, and the updater must run with write access to the installed module.

descriptions.description: CWE-94 Improper Control of Generation of Code

cna.title: JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's serialisation grows the Perl stack under allow_tags in encode_rv

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's serialisation grows the Perl stack under allow_tags in encode_rv.

With allow_tags, an object's FREEZE method is called in list context and each returned value is encoded through a saved Perl stack pointer. When encoding a returned value calls back into Perl, through TO_JSON under convert_blessed or another FREEZE, and that callback grows the stack, the stack is reallocated while the saved pointer still refers to the freed block.

Encoding such objects reads freed memory, and encode can return undef without an error.

cna.title: Guard Core: Unvalidated X-Forwarded-For-derived string used as a Redis key component and interpolated into a KEYS glob pattern

descriptions.value: Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, _extract_from_forwarded_header() in guard_core/utils.py returns the selected X-Forwarded-For entry without validating that it is an IP address. In deployments configured with trusted_proxies where the selected entry is attacker-controlled, the arbitrary client_ip string reaches BehaviorTracker in guard_core/handlers/behavior_handler.py and is interpolated into Redis key names and blocking KEYS glob patterns. Glob metacharacters can cause one request to count other clients' behavior events, embedded separators can disturb key parsing, and rotating identities can create unbounded keys while repeatedly scanning the shared Redis keyspace. A non-IP identity can also reach a ban action and cause an uncaught validation error. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

cna.title: Apache log4net: Culture-sensitive CDATA end search in XmlLayout hides later log events

descriptions.value:
Improper Output Neutralization for Logs vulnerability in the XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J of Apache log4net.

Both layouts split a message holding the CDATA end marker into several CDATA sections, but searched for the marker with a culture-sensitive comparison. Ignorable characters or a combining mark around the marker made the search miss it, so the CDATA section stayed open. From 3.3.1 on, an XML parser then reads the following log events as part of that message; earlier versions leave the log file not well-formed. A party whose data reaches a log message could hide later log events from a consumer that parses the XML log.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

ai_annotations.description: Draft vulnerability metadata was generated from a git-format patch using an Ollama-hosted language model. Human validation is required before publication.

x_patch2vuln.subject: fix: [security] A feed key or an API key no longer opens a
x_patch2vuln.fixSummary: The authentication decorators for feed-key and API-key requests no longer call Flask-Login's login_user(), which was writing the authenticated user into the session cookie and creating a full web session. Instead, the user object is now stored on Flask's request-scoped g._login_user attribute, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads first. This authenticates only the current request without setting any session cookie, preventing a limited-scope token from being elevated to a persistent, all-pages session that bypasses password and two-factor authentication.
assumptions: The application is assumed to be a self-hosted or publicly accessible web service; the patch does not specify deployment topology.
No specific version numbers are available from the patch; the affected version range is unspecified.

The CVSS sub-component impact (SC:H, SI:H) assumes the worst case where the authenticated account has administrative privileges, granting access to /admin. For non-admin accounts, the impact is limited to the user's own account data.
The CAPEC-63 mapping is the closest available match; no CAPEC precisely describes a limited-scope token being elevated to a full session via an improper login_user() call.

The commit message notes that pre-existing sessions created before the fix remain valid until expiration and are not bound to the credential (CWE-613); this is acknowledged as a separate issue not addressed by this patch.

The 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5' credit is included as a tool credit based on the explicit commit message; it is unclear whether this represents meaningful remediation contribution or automated assistance.
The patch does not indicate whether the application requires TLS or any other transport-level protection; CVSS assumes standard network access.
x_patch2vuln.patchSummary: In website/decorators.py (auth_feedkey_func) and website/web/api/v1/common.py (auth_func), the import of login_user from flask_login is removed and replaced with an import of g from flask. The call login_user(user) (or login_user(user, remember=False)) is replaced with g._login_user = user. A new test file tests/test_token_auth_no_session.py is added with four test cases verifying that: (1) a feed-key request returns 200 but sets no session cookie, (2) an API-key request returns 200 but sets no session cookie, (3) a subsequent unauthenticated request to /user/profile is redirected (302), and (4) a 403 response from an API-key request also sets no session cookie.
x_patch2vuln.cvssRationale: AV:N: The feed key is in a URL and the API key is in a header; both are accessible over the network. AC:L: A single HTTP request with the token is sufficient; no race conditions or special timing required. AT:N: No manipulation of the target system is needed. PR:N: No prior authentication is required; the token itself is the credential, and it is not protected by any additional gate. UI:N: No user interaction is needed. VC/VI/VA:N: The vulnerable component (the authentication layer) is not itself compromised in terms of its own data, integrity, or availability. SC:H: The attacker gains full read access to the user's account data, including the API key and profile information. SI:H: The attacker can modify the user's account settings, and for administrator accounts, can perform arbitrary administrative actions via /admin. SA:N: No availability impact on the user's account or the application is demonstrated by the evidence.

capecRationale.rationale: The feed key and API key are trusted credentials for specific, limited-scope access (feed delivery, API calls). The vulnerable implementation incorrectly leveraged that trust to establish a full web session, extending the credential's authority beyond its intended scope. This is the closest CAPEC to the pattern of a limited credential being used to gain broader access than intended. Uncertainty: no CAPEC precisely describes 'token authentication creating an unintended persistent session'; CAPEC-63 is the best available match for trust-scope escalation.

modelComparison.selectionNotice: The selected result is closest to model consensus; this heuristic does not establish factual correctness and human review remains required.

weaknessRationale.rationale: The authentication mechanism improperly elevated a limited-scope credential (feed key or API key intended for single-request authentication) into a full web session via login_user(), bypassing password and two-factor authentication. The authentication check succeeded but the session establishment was incorrect for the credential type.

The commit message explicitly references CWE-613 as a related concern: sessions created before the fix remain valid until they expire and are not bound to the original credential. While the primary fix addresses the session creation, the lack of credential binding in existing sessions is a secondary weakness acknowledged by the developers.

events.description: Vulnerability report received by e-mail from the reporter.
Report reproduced: a feed key or an API key opens a full web session, which also bypasses two-factor authentication.
Corrective change authored (3605d5b6): a feed key or an API key no longer opens a web session.
Fix pushed to the public main branch.

descriptions.value: CAPEC-63 Leverage Trusted Relationships

solutions.value: The authentication decorators for feed-key and API-key requests no longer call Flask-Login's login_user(), which was writing the authenticated user into the session cookie and creating a full web session. Instead, the user object is now stored on Flask's request-scoped g._login_user attribute, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads first. This authenticates only the current request without setting any session cookie, preventing a limited-scope token from being elevated to a persistent, all-pages session that bypasses password and two-factor authentication.

descriptions.value:
In the vulnerability-lookup web application, the authentication decorators for feed-key requests (auth_feedkey_func in website/decorators.py) and API-key requests (auth_func in website/web/api/v1/common.py) called Flask-Login's login_user() function. This caused the HTTP response to a request authenticated solely by a feed key (supplied as the X-FEED-KEY URL parameter) or an API key (supplied as the X-API-KEY header) to set a session cookie that grants full authenticated access to every page in the application, without requiring a password or two-factor authentication.

The practical impact is that any party possessing a leaked feed URL (a common occurrence, as feed URLs are shared with RSS readers) or an API key could obtain a valid web session for the associated account. This session provides access to the user's account page, which exposes the API key and other profile data, and for accounts with the administrator role, access to the /admin interface, enabling full administrative control of the application.

The vulnerability affects all users whose feed key or API key is exposed. No prior authentication, user interaction, or special network conditions are required; a single HTTP request with the token is sufficient to establish the session. The session persists until it expires, and because it is not bound to the original credential (a related CWE-613 issue noted by the developers), revoking the feed key or API key does not invalidate the already-created session.

The fix replaces the login_user() call with assignment to g._login_user, which Flask-Login's current_user property reads for the current request only, without writing any session cookie. The affected views remain unchanged and continue to see the authenticated user for the single request.

cna.title: bgpd: out-of-bounds heap read and crash on NOTIFICATION Cease/Hard Reset with one data byte

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

solutions.value: Upgrade to a fixed version of FRRouting

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to a fixed version of FRRouting

workarounds.value: Graceful Restart Capability needs to be enabled. Disable the Capability with "no bgp graceful-restart notification" or "bgp graceful-restart-disable"

supportingMedia.value: Graceful Restart Capability needs to be enabled. Disable the Capability with "no bgp graceful-restart notification" or "bgp graceful-restart-disable"

descriptions.value: In FRRouting (FRR) 8.3 through 10.5.1, bgp_notify_decapsulate_hard_reset() in bgpd/bgp_packet.c does not validate the length of the data field of a received BGP NOTIFICATION Cease/Hard Reset message (RFC 8538). When the data field is exactly one byte long, the function reads one byte past the end of a heap buffer and the 16-bit length of the encapsulated data underflows to 65535, causing a 65535-byte out-of-bounds heap read followed by an assertion failure. A remote BGP peer that has established a session and negotiated the Graceful Restart capability with the Notification (N) bit can send such a message to crash the bgpd daemon, terminating all BGP sessions (denial of service). This is fixed in 10.0.5, 10.1.5, 10.2.6, 10.3.4, 10.4.3, 10.5.2 and 10.6.0.

supportingMedia.value: In FRRouting (FRR) 8.3 through 10.5.1, bgp_notify_decapsulate_hard_reset() in bgpd/bgp_packet.c does not validate the length of the data field of a received BGP NOTIFICATION Cease/Hard Reset message (RFC 8538). When the data field is exactly one byte long, the function reads one byte past the end of a heap buffer and the 16-bit length of the encapsulated data underflows to 65535, causing a 65535-byte out-of-bounds heap read followed by an assertion failure. A remote BGP peer that has established a session and negotiated the Graceful Restart capability with the Notification (N) bit can send such a message to crash the bgpd daemon, terminating all BGP sessions (denial of service). This is fixed in 10.0.5, 10.1.5, 10.2.6, 10.3.4, 10.4.3, 10.5.2 and 10.6.0.

configurations.value: bgpd must be running with at least one BGP neighbor (or dynamic listen range) through which the attacker can establish a session, and the Graceful Restart capability with the Notification (N) bit must be negotiated in the OPEN exchange with that peer. This is the default configuration: "bgp graceful-restart notification" is enabled by default since FRR 8.3 and the Graceful Restart capability is advertised by default (helper mode). Instances configured with "no bgp graceful-restart notification" or "bgp graceful-restart-disable" are not affected.

cna.title: Kubeshark: MCP `download_file` writes fetched bytes to an unvalidated destination path

descriptions.value: Kubeshark is an eBPF-powered network observability tool for Kubernetes. From 53.1.0 until 53.4.0, the download_file tool in cmd/mcpRunner.go accepts caller-controlled path and dest values, fetches a selected Kubeshark Hub API response, and writes the returned bytes through os.Create(dest) in callDownloadFile without confining the destination. An attacker who influences arguments through an AI agent driving kubeshark mcp can write Hub-supplied bytes to any path writable by the local MCP user and can read captured network traffic from default auth-disabled Hub deployments. The tool is registered without --allow-destructive; reliable code execution is not demonstrated because the bytes are constrained to Hub API responses. Hub-side default authentication remains outside this remediation, so captured traffic can remain readable in default auth-disabled Hub deployments after the local destination-write fix. The destination-write issue is fixed in version 53.4.0.

cna.title: Double free during DOM XML serialization

descriptions.value: CAPEC-123 Buffer Manipulation

Double free during DOM XML serialization.

The XML serializer of Dom\XMLDocument and Dom\HTMLDocument can share ownership of a generated namespace prefix between the namespace-prefix maps of an element and a descendant, so the prefix is used after being freed and then freed a second time. The document does not need to be malformed. An application that parses attacker-controlled XML or HTML with these classes and serializes it with saveXml() can be crashed, and repeated requests can cause denial of service. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution

descriptions.value: CAPEC-123 Buffer Manipulation

Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Prior to 3.10.4, the semantic-logic read_type parser recursively processes both halves of nested complex type strings without applying LogicParser.MAX_PARSE_DEPTH. An attacker-controlled type string or signature with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through Type.fromstring or type-checking entry points and abort the current worker. cna.title: mail-parser: Uncaught `OverflowError` / `OSError` on an out-of-range `Received` date

descriptions.value: mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 3.7.0 until 4.6.3, receiveds_format() in src/mailparser/utils.py catches only TypeError and ValueError while converting the trailing date of an attacker-controlled Received header. An out-of-range year can cause calendar.timegm() to raise OverflowError, and a sufficiently large timezone offset can cause datetime.fromtimestamp() to raise OSError. These exceptions are outside the MailParserError hierarchy, so one crafted header can abort the entire message parse through every parse_from_* entry point and may drop a queued batch. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.3.

The result is disclosure of sensitive information to parties whose access to error output is broader than their intended access to the configuration secret.

cna.title: PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body

descriptions.value: CAPEC-33 HTTP Request Smuggling

PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: libspdm: libspdm_x509_verify_cert_chain() does not verify CA nameConstraints / pathLenConstraint

descriptions.value: libspdm is a sample implementation that follows the DMTF SPDM specifications. Prior to 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2, libspdm_x509_verify_cert_chain() in os_stub/cryptlib_openssl/pk/x509.c and os_stub/cryptlib_mbedtls/pk/x509.c validates certificate signatures one link at a time instead of validating the complete X.509 path. In deployments using a pinned root with a constrained multi-tier PKI, an attacker holding a valid issuer credential below a constrained CA can present a subordinate certificate that exceeds pathLenConstraint or nameConstraints and may be accepted for SPDM identity validation. Exploitation requires the application to use libspdm's backend validation without an additional certificate-chain validation mechanism, the pinned root cannot be substituted, and the deployment's measurement policy must allow identity impersonation alone to satisfy its acceptance requirements. The mbedTLS backend remains unable to enforce nameConstraints because upstream mbedTLS does not implement that check. The full-chain validation changes are released in versions 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2.

cna.title: frr: bgpd use-after-free of Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs via the attribute intern reuse cache with soft-reconfiguration inbound

workarounds.value: Remove "neighbor <neighbor> soft-reconfiguration inbound", or configure "neighbor <neighbor> path-attribute discard 23" (or "neighbor <neighbor> path-attribute treat-as-withdraw 23") for neighbors that are not expected to send the Tunnel Encapsulation attribute, in particular all eBGP neighbors. With the attribute discarded, bgpd skips it without parsing or storing it.

descriptions.value: In FRRouting, bgpd frees the sub-TLV chain of a Tunnel Encapsulation attribute (type 23) while routes stored by bgpd still point to it, if the attribute is received from a neighbor that has "soft-reconfiguration inbound" configured. A cache added to speed up attribute interning while processing the prefixes of an UPDATE checks whether an interned attribute set may be reused by comparing the parsed attributes with themselves, so the check always succeeds. Interning the parsed attributes for the Adj-RIB-In removes the Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLVs from them, and the copy that bgpd then interns for the route reuses the cached attribute set, which still holds the sub-TLVs, without taking a reference on them. When the route is later replaced, withdrawn or cleared, for example when the session goes down, the sub-TLV chain is freed while still in use, and bgpd then reads it, decrements a reference count inside it and frees it a second time. In the reporter's build without AddressSanitizer this ended in an assertion failure in bgpd's memory accounting, aborting bgpd and dropping all BGP sessions on the router, and the neighbor can repeat it each time bgpd restarts. Because freed heap memory is written to and freed again, consequences beyond a crash cannot be ruled out. An established BGP session is required, and the attribute does not need to be malformed. bgpd processes attribute 23 from every neighbor, including eBGP neighbors, unless it is explicitly discarded, although RFC 9012 requires it to be filtered on eBGP sessions by default. Neighbors without "soft-reconfiguration inbound" are not affected.

descriptions.description: CWE-416 Use After Free: the attribute intern reuse cache returns an interned attribute set holding the Tunnel Encapsulation sub-TLV chain without taking a reference on the chain, which is then freed while still referenced and later accessed by encap_unintern()

cna.title: NLTK: Uncontrolled recursion in CCG lexicon parser causes denial of service via deeply nested category input

descriptions.value: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the CCG lexicon parser's matchBrackets and augParseCategory functions recursively process nested parenthesized categories without a depth bound. An attacker-controlled lexicon string with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through nltk.ccg.lexicon.fromstring and terminate the parse operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

cna.title: JSON::XS versions from 4.0_00 before 4.05 for Perl corrupt the incremental buffer length by chopping past its end in incr_skip after a top-level number

solutions.value: Upgrade to JSON-XS 4.05 or later.

descriptions.value:
JSON::XS versions from 4.0_00 before 4.05 for Perl corrupt the incremental buffer length by chopping past its end in incr_skip after a top-level number.

The incremental parser scans any run of digits, signs, dots and exponent markers as one number, but the decoder stops at the end of a valid number, so the parser keeps an offset into bytes it has not decoded. It then empties the buffer without clearing those bytes, and a later incr_parse call without new input reads them again and moves the offset past the end of the buffer. incr_skip, the documented recovery after an error, removes that many bytes and the buffer length wraps.

A peer sending input such as "1-2" to an incr_parse consumer can make the next read of incr_text exit the process through perl's uncatchable out-of-memory path.

cna.title: Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input

descriptions.value: CAPEC-92 Forced Integer Overflow

Incorrect RFC 3986 URI serialization for oversized input.

The Uri\Rfc3986\Uri class does not correctly handle the output-size limit and errors of the uriparser library when converting a URI back to a string. For a URI whose string representation reaches approximately 2 GiB, toString(), toRawString() and other serializing operations can return a truncated or invalid string instead of an error. An application that accepts attacker-controlled URI data of that size, has enough memory to process it and trusts the result may make incorrect validation or routing decisions, and the large allocations can exhaust memory. parse_url() and Uri\WhatWg\Url are not affected.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

cna.title: Insecure deserializaiton in the httpx Ruby gem via unsafe Oj object-mode

credits.value: Natan Nehorai of the JFrog Vulnerability Research team

scenarios.value: An application loads oj before httpx, does not have multi_json in its bundle, does not pin a safe process-wide Oj.default_options, the Ruby process contains a valid gadget chain, and calls response.json on a response from an attacker-influenced URL.

timeline.value: JFrog reports the issue to the httpx maintainer via email.
Maintainer commits the fix (eeb785d) changing json_load to use Oj :strict mode; released as httpx v1.9.1.

solutions.value: Upgrade to httpx 1.9.1, which calls Oj.load with an explicit { mode: :strict } default. If upgrading is not possible, pass a safe mode at the call site (response.json(mode: :strict)), or set a safe process-wide default such as Oj.default_options = { mode: :strict } (or :rails) before any untrusted JSON is parsed. Do not rely on Oj's shipped :object default for data that arrived over the network.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to httpx 1.9.1, which calls Oj.load with an explicit { mode: :strict } default. If upgrading is not possible, pass a safe mode at the call site (response.json(mode: :strict)), or set a safe process-wide default such as Oj.default_options = { mode: :strict } (or :rails) before any untrusted JSON is parsed. Do not rely on Oj's shipped :object default for data that arrived over the network.

references.name: Fix commit: json: fix oj integration to avoid RCE mode
Oj security documentation: :object mode and safe loading

descriptions.value: The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

Reaching code execution additionally requires a gadget chain and an attacker-influenced URL passed to response.json. Applications that keep multi_json, pin a safe Oj mode, or call response.json with an explicit safe mode are not exploitable.

cna.title: Apache log4net: AdoNetAppender loses an event whose text the database cannot store

descriptions.value:
Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character vulnerability in the AdoNetAppender of Apache log4net.

Text parameters were bound unchanged, so a NUL character or an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate reached the database as it was. A database that refuses such a value, such as PostgreSQL, rejected the insert and the event was lost; only the first such loss per appender was reported. A party whose data reaches a log message could suppress that event.

This issue affects Apache log4net: from 1.2.9 before 3.6.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.6.0, which fixes the issue.

cna.title: Apache Shiro: DefaultLdapRealm accepts any password when authentication caching is enabled

descriptions.value:
When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

cna.title: qbee-agent: Docker Compose build context Zip Slip writes outside context directory

descriptions.value: qbee-agent is the device agent component of the qbee.io IoT device management platform. Prior to 2026.41, the unpackTar extraction logic in app/utils/tar.go validates cleaned archive entry paths with strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, destdirClean) without enforcing a path-separator boundary. When UseContext enables the Docker Compose build context path in app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose.go, a less-privileged archive supplier with delegated configuration and/or file-manager access can provide a sibling-prefix traversal entry that passes the check, causing utils.UnpackTar to create directories and regular files outside the intended context extraction directory with qbee-agent process privileges, despite the supplier lacking authority to write those sibling files. In deployments where only full device or fleet administrators can provide Docker Compose context archives, this behavior is hardening rather than a crossed security boundary. The demonstrated impact is limited to nearby cache or project paths sharing the destination prefix, may affect integrity or availability of qbee-agent-managed Docker Compose state, and does not establish arbitrary absolute-path writes or direct code execution. This issue is fixed in version 2026.41.

  query with a non-matching `live-channel-condition` is returned without filtering it by the policy (3.0.0 to 3.9.8). This allows an authenticated user to read Thing fields they are not allowed to read, in
  some cases without any permission on the Thing.

descriptions.value: The MongoDB Go Driver does not neutralize NUL characters in the user name and password values it places into the message it builds for SASL PLAIN authentication. A party who can choose the login values that an application passes to the driver can alter where the fields of that message begin and end. This may result in a receiving system reading a login name and secret that differ from the values the application supplied. Authenticating as a different account still requires that account's password. Only deployments that use SASL PLAIN authentication are affected.

Prior to 3.10.4, Prover9Parent.config_prover9 and Mace accept a relative binary_location and pass it to find_binary as path_to_bin, disabling the bare-name absolute-path guard. descriptions.value: In Eclipse Ditto versions before 3.8.15 and 3.9.0 to 3.9.8, the policy enforcers do not let a revoke win over a grant in two kinds of permission checks. Checks of several permissions at once compare the highest grant weight with the highest revoke weight across all requested permissions instead of per permission, so the "check permissions" API (`POST /api/2/checkPermissions`, available since 3.7.0) can report a set of permissions as granted although one of them is revoked. Partial permission checks, which authorize retrieving Things and Policies and determine the receivers of events, count a grant on a sub-resource although the same permission is revoked on that sub-resource for another subject of the same authorization context (or, with the memory-optimized policy evaluator, for the same subject). A requester can thereby learn about the existence of Things and Policies and receive metadata without any readable content, and an application relying on the check permissions result may grant access the policy denies. The content of retrieved Things and Policies is still filtered correctly, and modifications are not affected.

cna.title: mail-parser: One hostile attachment aborts `write_attachments()` and silently drops the rest of the batch

descriptions.value: mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.6.0 until 4.6.3, write_attachments() calls _safe_attachment_filename() and write_sample() without isolating failures for individual attacker-controlled MIME parts. An RFC 2231 filename containing a NUL, a basename exceeding NAME_MAX, or an undecodable base64 payload can raise ValueError, OSError, or binascii.Error and abort the entire save loop. Later attachments remain unwritten; when a caller catches only MailParserError, the failure is not surfaced through the expected library-exception path. If a downstream scanner or sandbox reads only the extraction directory, a payload after the crafted part can be missed even though it remains in the delivered message, and the aborted batch also causes availability loss. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.3.

cna.title: mail-parser is vulnerable to polynomial ReDoS in email header parsing

descriptions.value: mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. From 4.2.0 until 4.6.1, attacker-controlled email headers can cause polynomial regular-expression backtracking during ordinary parse_from_string(), parse_from_bytes(), or parse_from_file() calls. In src/mailparser/utils.py, get_addresses() invokes the _ADDR_FALLBACK_RE fallback when strict address parsing yields no usable address, and overlapping quantifiers rescan padded address headers quadratically or cubically. In src/mailparser/const.py, parse_received() applies _CLAUSE_SPLITTER to uncollapsed whitespace in a Received header, causing quadratic backtracking when a whitespace run is not followed by a clause keyword. A small, well-formed message can keep mail gateway, ticketing, quarantine, or archival parsing workers busy for extended periods. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.1.

descriptions.value: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

cna.title: Possible Heap Buffer Overflow in ASN.1 Multibyte String Conversion

descriptions.value:
Issue summary: A signed integer overflow when sizing the destination
buffer for Unicode output in ASN1_mbstring_ncopy() can lead to a heap
buffer overflow.

Impact summary: A heap buffer overflow may lead to a crash or possibly
attacker controlled code execution or other undefined behaviour.

In ASN1_mbstring_copy() and ASN1_mbstring_ncopy() the destination
size for Unicode output is computed in a signed int: by left shift
of the input character count for BMPSTRING (UTF-16) and
UNIVERSALSTRING (UTF-32), and by summing per-character byte counts
for UTF8STRING. The calculation overflows when the input reaches
around 2^30 characters. In the worst case (UNIVERSALSTRING at 2^30
characters) the size wraps to zero, OPENSSL_malloc(1) is called, and
the subsequent character copy writes several gigabytes past the
one-byte allocation.

X.509 certificate processing routes through ASN1_STRING_set_by_NID(),
whose DIRSTRING_TYPE mask excludes UNIVERSALSTRING and whose per-NID
size limits cap the input length; no network protocol or
certificate-handling path in OpenSSL exercises the overflow.
Triggering the bug requires an application that calls
ASN1_mbstring_copy() or ASN1_mbstring_ncopy() directly, or registers
a custom string type via ASN1_STRING_TABLE_add(), with
attacker-controlled input on the order of half a gigabyte or more.
For these reasons this issue was assigned Low severity.

The FIPS modules in 4.0, 3.6, 3.5, 3.4 and 3.0 are not affected by
this issue, as the affected code is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module
boundary.

cna.title: Ollama heap out-of-bounds read in GGUF tensor parsing leaks server process memory to unauthenticated remote attackers

credits.value: Cyera Research Team (Dor Attias, Ofek Itach)

descriptions.value: CAPEC-540 Overread Buffers

solutions.value: Upgrade to ollama 0.17.1 or later. The fix in PR #14406 validates that declared tensor offset+size do not exceed the GGUF file size before reading, and adds a length check in the quantizer prior to the unsafe read.

supportingMedia.value: Upgrade to ollama 0.17.1 or later. The fix in PR #14406 validates that declared tensor offset+size do not exceed the GGUF file size before reading, and adds a length check in the quantizer prior to the unsafe read.

references.name: ollama/ollama PR #14406 — ggml: ensure tensor size is valid (fix)

workarounds.value: Until upgrade is possible: (1) ensure Ollama is bound to a trusted interface only (default OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1); (2) front Ollama with a reverse proxy that requires authentication on /api/create and /api/push; (3) restrict outbound network egress from the Ollama host to prevent exfiltration via /api/push to attacker-controlled registries.

supportingMedia.value: Until upgrade is possible: (1) ensure Ollama is bound to a trusted interface only (default OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1); (2) front Ollama with a reverse proxy that requires authentication on /api/create and /api/push; (3) restrict outbound network egress from the Ollama host to prevent exfiltration via /api/push to attacker-controlled registries.

descriptions.value: Ollama before 0.17.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the GGUF model loader. The /api/create endpoint accepts an attacker-supplied GGUF file in which the declared tensor offset and size exceed the file's actual length; during quantization in fs/ggml/gguf.go and server/quantization.go (WriteTo()), the server reads past the allocated heap buffer. The leaked memory contents may include environment variables, API keys, system prompts, and concurrent users' conversation data, and can be exfiltrated by uploading the resulting model artifact through the /api/push endpoint to an attacker-controlled registry. The /api/create and /api/push endpoints have no authentication in the upstream distribution. Default deployments bind to 127.0.0.1, but the documented OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 configuration is widely used in practice (large public-internet exposure observed).

This vulnerability allows an authenticated OpenShift user with edit permissions in a single namespace to exploit improper symlink validation when connecting to virtual machine console sockets. By replacing the console socket with a symlink to the host's container runtime (CRI-O) socket, an attacker can hijack virt-handler's privileged connection. This enables the attacker to access any Unix socket on the host, potentially leading to full control of the node and the entire cluster.

cna.title: pgAdmin 4: Cross-user data access and shared-server privilege escalation in server mode

scenarios.value: Multi-tenant pgAdmin in server mode where authenticated users have legitimate access to their own resources but should not access others'. Cross-user access to private servers, processes, and debugger state is a genuine scope change (each user is a distinct security authority within pgAdmin); shared-server passexec_cmd write yields RCE in the owner's process context. 9.9 reflects the worst-case multi-tenant deployment.

Multi-tenant pgAdmin in server mode where authenticated users have legitimate access to their own resources but should not access others'. Cross-user access to private servers, processes, and debugger state is a genuine scope change (each user is a distinct security authority within pgAdmin); shared-server passexec_cmd write yields RCE in the owner's process context. 9.9 reflects the worst-case multi-tenant deployment.

descriptions.value:
Authorization vulnerability in pgAdmin 4 server mode affecting Server Groups, Servers, Shared Servers, Background Processes, and Debugger modules.

Multiple endpoints fetched user-owned objects without filtering by the requesting user's identity. An authenticated user could access another user's private servers, server groups, background processes, and debugger function arguments by guessing object IDs.

Additionally, the Shared Servers feature contained multiple issues including credential leakage (passexec_cmd, passfile, SSL keys), privilege escalation via writable passexec_cmd (a shell command executed when establishing the connection) allowing arbitrary command execution in the owner's process context, and owner-data corruption via SQLAlchemy session mutations. Several owner-only fields (passexec_cmd, passexec_expiration, db_res, db_res_type) were writable by non-owners through the API, and additional fields (kerberos_conn, tags, post_connection_sql) lacked per-user persistence so non-owner edits mutated the owner's record.

Fix centralises access control via a new server_access module, scopes all user-owned models with a UserScopedMixin, returns HTTP 410 from connection_manager when access is denied in server mode, suppresses owner-only fields for non-owners across the merge / API response / ServerManager paths, and adds an explicit owner-only write guard. The remediation landed in two pull requests; both are referenced.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.15.

adp.title: assisted-service: assisted-service: Authenticated users can gain administrative access to OpenShift clusters via credential disclosure

solutions.value: RHSA-2026:12337: multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.11
RHSA-2026:12116: multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.1
RHSA-2026:11511: multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.7
RHSA-2026:11512: multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.7
RHSA-2026:18584: multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.9
RHSA-2026:18585: multicluster engine for Kubernetes 2.9

descriptions.value:
A vulnerability in the assisted-service REST API, an optional Assisted Installer (assisted-service) component in the Multicluster Engine (MCE), allows an authenticated user with minimal namespace-scoped privileges to obtain administrative credentials for arbitrary clusters provisioned through the hub. 

The credentials download endpoint (GET /v2/clusters/{cluster_id}/credentials, which returns the kubeadmin password) and the kubeconfig download endpoint are operational in AUTH_TYPE=local mode, the only authentication mode available in on-premises ACM/MCE hub deployments. The local authenticator unconditionally grants full administrative access to any request bearing a valid JWT, with no per-endpoint restrictions. A valid local JWT is embedded as a plaintext query parameter in InfraEnvStatus.ISODownloadURL and is readable by any user who has get rights on an InfraEnv object in their own namespace.

The affected components ship as part of Multicluster Engine (MCE). The Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (ACM) deployments that include MCE are equally affected.
This issue does not affect the hosted SaaS offering (console.redhat.com), which uses a different authentication mode.

Successful exploitation gives the attacker the kubeadmin password and kubeconfig for any OpenShift cluster provisioned through the affected hub, granting unrestricted root-level administrative access to those spoke clusters.

cna.title: Arista EOS Unexpected Tunnel Protocol Decapsulation and Forwarding Bypass

credits.value: Scott Christiansen, Lukas Peitz, Rich Compton, and Jonathan Davis at Comcast

descriptions.value: CAPEC-272 Protocol Abuse

solutions.value: No software upgrade path is planned to address this issue due to the risk of breaking existing configuration on deployments. The recommended resolution of this issue is to follow the appropriate mitigation instructions detailed in the workaround block.

supportingMedia.value: No software upgrade path is planned to address this issue due to the risk of breaking existing configuration on deployments. The recommended resolution of this issue is to follow the appropriate mitigation instructions detailed in the workaround block.

workarounds.value:
There are two broad approaches to mitigate this issue - (1) applying ACLs on upstream devices or (2) applying ACLs on the devices where the unexpected decapsulation is happening. In both cases, the idea is to either selectively allow only legitimate tunnel traffic or to selectively block malicious tunnel traffic. For example, if a network is configured to forward VXLAN traffic, but GRE traffic is being unexpectedly forwarded, then ACLs can be used to either selectively allow just VXLAN traffic or selectively block GRE traffic. More details about using the ACL feature can be found in the  Arista User Manual https://www.arista.com/en/um-eos/eos-acls-and-route-maps#xx1150869 .



A note of caution, the following ACL-based mitigation recommendations assume that the tunnel IP is dedicated solely to receiving the configured tunnel protocol traffic. When adapting these rules for your environment, it is important to explicitly permit any additional protocol traffic—such as BGP or SSH—if that IP serves multiple functions. To maintain connectivity, ensure these permit statements are sequenced before any deny statements directed at the decapsulation IP.



The following configurations align with the recommendations outlined in the  Arista EOS Hardening Guide https://arista.my.site.com/AristaCommunity/s/article/arista-eos-hardening-guide#Comm_Kna_ka0Uw00000097VJIAY_71 .

workarounds.value:
Approach 1 - Applying ACL on Upstream Switches

On upstream devices, applying ACLs to allow specific tunneled traffic is straightforward. ACLs can be applied that match on tunnel destination IP, the IP next protocol field, and (optionally) UDP destination port to selectively allow or block specific tunnel protocols.



Example ACLs for Arista EOS follows.

ACL to permit VXLANv4 Only

This IPv4 ACL matches on VXLAN packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = UDP (17)
(b) IP DIP = VXLAN VTEP IP
(c) UDP destination port = VXLAN UDP Port (4789)



It allows VXLAN packets and drops all other packets to the VXLAN Decap IP.



ip access-list foo
   counters per-entry
   1 permit udp any host <vxlan-decap-ip> eq 4789
   2 deny ip any host <decap-ip>
   3 permit ip any any


 

ACL to permit GREv4 Only

This IPv4 ACL matches on GRE packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = GRE (47)
(b) IP DIP = GRE Tunnel Destination IP



It allows GRE packets and drops all other packets to the GRE Decap IP.



ip access-list foo
   counters per-entry
   1 permit gre any host <gre-decap-ip>
   2 deny ip any host <gre-decap-ip>
   3 permit any any


 

ACL to permit IP-in-IPv4 Only

This IPv4 ACL matches on IP-in-IPv4 packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = IPv4 (4) or IPv6 (41)
(b) IP DIP = IP-in-IP Decap IP



It allows IP-in-IPv4 packets and drops all other packets to the IP-in-IPv4 Decap IP.



ip access-list foo
   counters per-entry
   1 permit 4 any host <ipip-decap-ip>
   2 permit 41 any host <ipip-decap-ip>
   3 deny ip any host <ipip-decap-ip>
   4 permit any any


 

ACL to Permit IP-in-IPv6 Only

This IPv6 ACL matches on IP-in-IPv6 packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = IPv4 (4) or IPv6 (41)
(b) IP DIP = IP-in-IP Decap IP



It allows IP-in-IPv6 packets and drops all other packets to the IP-in-IPv6 Decap IP.



ipv6 access-list foo
   counters per-entry
   1 permit 4 any host <ipip-decap-ip>
   2 permit 41 any host <ipip-decap-ip>
   3 deny ipv6 any host <ipip-decap-ip>
   4 permit ipv6 any any


 

ACL to permit GUEv4 Only

This IPv4 ACL matches on GUE packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = UDP (17)
(b) IP DIP = GUE Decap IP
(c) UDP destination port = UDP port configured per payload
       (IP = Y or MPLS = Z)



It allows GUE packets and drops all other packets to the GUE Decap IP.



ip access-list foo
   counters per-entry
   1 permit udp any host <decap-ip> eq Y
   2 permit udp any host <decap-ip> eq Z
   3 deny ip any host <decap-ip>
   4 permit ip any any


 

ACL to Permit GUEv6 Only

This IPv6 ACL matches on GUE packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = UDP (17)
(b) IP DIP = GUE Decap IP
(c) UDP destination port = UDP port configured per payload
       (IP = Y or MPLS = Z)



It allows GUE packets and drops all other packets to the GUE Decap IP.



ipv6 access-list foo
   counters per-entry
   1 permit udp any host <decap-ip> eq Y
   2 permit udp any host <decap-ip> eq Z
   3 deny ipv6 any host <decap-ip>
   4 permit ipv6 any any

workarounds.value:
Approach 2 - Applying ACL on Decapsulation Switches

Applying ACLs on the decapsulation device is more complicated. It requires the use of MAC ACLs on 7020R Series, 7280R/R2 Series, and 7500R/R2 Series systems and IP ACLs on 7280R3 Series, 7500R3 Series, and 7800R3 Series systems. In both cases, a TCAM profile update is also required. Note that TCAM profile update is a disruptive operation that could impact traffic forwarding. More information can be found in  User-defined TCAM Profiles https://www.arista.com/en/support/toi/eos-4-26-0f/14755-user-defined-tcam-profiles .

7020R Series, 7280R/R2 Series, and 7500R/R2 Series

Mitigation involves using MAC ACLs to allow specific expected protocol packets and block all other traffic to the configured decap IPs. The suggested MAC ACLs use User Defined Fields (UDFs) to match on specific fields in the packet headers. This requires a TCAM profile update to include the following UDF qualifiers:

  *  For IPv4 tunnels, 2 16b and 1 32b UDF qualifiers need to be included.
  *  For IPv6 tunnels, 2 16b and 4 32b UDF qualifiers need to be included.


However, in order to make room for the UDF qualifiers, other TCAM features/qualifiers must be removed due to hardware constraints. Following are some suggested TCAM profile changes to accommodate the required UDF qualifiers:

  *  TCAM profile that includes the UDF qualifiers for IPv4 tunnels, but removes support for MPLS:


hardware tcam
   profile test copy default
      feature acl port mac
         no key size limit 
         key field udf-16b-1 udf-16b-2 udf-32b-1
      no feature mpls
      no feature mpls pop ingress
      no feature pbr mpls


 

 
  *  TCAM profile that includes the UDF qualifiers for IPv4 tunnels, but removes support for VXLAN:


hardware tcam
   profile test copy default
      feature acl port mac
         no key field src-mac
         key field udf-16b-1 udf-16b-2 udf-32b-1


 

  
  *  TCAM profile that includes the UDF qualifiers for IPv6 tunnels, but removes support for VXLAN and PBR:


hardware tcam
   profile test1 copy default
      feature acl port mac
         no key size limit
         no key field src-mac dst-mac
         key field udf-16b-1 udf-16b-2 udf-32b-1 udf-32b-2 udf-32b-3 udf-32b-4
      no feature tunnel vxlan
      no feature tunnel vxlan routing
      no feature pbr ip
      no feature pbr ipv6



 



Please contact Arista TAC if further assistance is needed with TCAM profile construction.

ACL to permit VXLAN v4 Decap only

This MAC ACL uses UDF to match on VXLAN packets as follows:
(a) IP next protocol = UDP (0x11)
(b) IP DIP = VXLAN VTEP IP (say 0xXXXXXXXX - converted in hex)
(c) UDP destination port = VXLAN UDP Port (0x12b5)



It allows VXLAN packets and drops all other packets to the VXLAN Decap IP.

mac access-list payload alias udp-dport-vxlan offset 5 pattern 0x000012b5 mask 0xffff0000

   counters per-entry

   2 deny any any ip payload alias ip-dip-decap-ip

descriptions.value:
On affected platforms running Arista EOS where a tunnel decapsulation configuration—such as VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN), decap-groups, or a GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation) tunnel interface—is present, the switch will incorrectly decapsulate and forward other unexpected tunneled packet with a destination IP matching its configured decapsulation IP. This occurs because the switch does not verify the tunnel protocol type, potentially leading to the unexpected processing of non-configured tunnel traffic.



This issue has been reported as being exploited in the wild.

The device must be configured as a tunnel endpoint with a decapsulation IP — for example, as a VXLAN VTEP, a GRE tunnel endpoint, or with an ip decap-group.

configurations.value:
To check if the device is acting as a VXLAN VTEP:



switch>show interfaces vxlan 1
 Vxlan1 is up, line protocol is up (connected)
   Source interface is Loopback1 and is active with 10.0.0.1
   Listening on UDP port 4789
   ...


 



If the output contains “Source interface is <interface> and is active with <IP>”, the device is acting as a VXLAN VTEP with <IP> as the tunnel termination address, and is potentially impacted.



To check if a GRE tunnel interface is configured:



switch>show interfaces Tunnel0
 Tunnel0 is up, line protocol is up
   Hardware is Tunnel
   Tunnel source 1.1.1.1, destination 1.1.1.2
   Tunnel protocol/transport GRE/IP
   ...


 



If the tunnel interface is up with a source and destination, the device is a GRE tunnel endpoint and is potentially impacted.



To check if decap-groups are configured:



switch>show ip decap-group


 



If none of the above outputs show the presence of any tunnel endpoint configurations, the device does not perform tunnel decapsulation and is not exposed to this issue.

If the output contains “Source interface is <interface> and is active with <IP>”, the device is acting as a VXLAN VTEP with <IP> as the tunnel termination address, and is potentially impacted.

To check if a GRE tunnel interface is configured:

switch>show interfaces Tunnel0
 Tunnel0 is up, line protocol is up
   Hardware is Tunnel
   Tunnel source 1.1.1.1, destination 1.1.1.2
   Tunnel protocol/transport GRE/IP
   ...
 

If the tunnel interface is up with a source and destination, the device is a GRE tunnel endpoint and is potentially impacted.

To check if decap-groups are configured:

switch>show ip decap-group
 

If none of the above outputs show the presence of any tunnel endpoint configurations, the device does not perform tunnel decapsulation and is not exposed to this issue.

cna.title: WP-Redirection <= 1.0.3 - Cross-Site Request Forgery to Settings Update

The function morse_dot11ah_find_s1g_caps_for_bssid() uses the IE length field directly as the size argument to memcpy without validating it against the 15-byte destination buffer. cna.title: Stack-based buffer overflow in FalkorDB _RdbLoadEntity via unbounded property count in crafted RDB

descriptions.value: CAPEC-100 Overflow Buffers

timeline.value: CVE ID shared with the vendor

solutions.value: Upgrade FalkorDB to version 4.18.4 or later.

workarounds.value: Require authentication on the Redis/FalkorDB instance (requirepass or ACLs), restrict or rename the REPLICAOF/SLAVEOF commands so untrusted clients cannot use them, and do not expose the instance to untrusted networks.

descriptions.value: A stack-based buffer overflow in the _RdbLoadEntity function of the RDB graph decoders (src/serializers/decoders/*/decode_graph_entities.c) in FalkorDB before 4.18.4 allows a remote attacker who can issue Redis replication commands (for example, against an instance with no password configured) to cause a denial of service and possibly execute arbitrary code by supplying a crafted RDB stream with an attacker-controlled entity property count. The count sizes two variable-length arrays on the thread stack with no upper bound, and the decoder then fills them with attacker-supplied values.

cna.title: UltraVNC MS-Logon II uses 64-bit Diffie-Hellman and seeded libc rand() enabling credential interception

descriptions.value: UltraVNC through 1.8.2.2 uses inadequate cryptography in the MS-Logon II authentication scheme (rfbUltraVNC_MsLogonIIAuth). In rfb/dh.cpp the Diffie-Hellman key exchange is performed with parameters that fit in an unsigned 64-bit integer (DH_MAX_BITS controls the prime size). A 64-bit DH key can be broken by Pollard's rho algorithm in under one second on current hardware. Additionally, the private exponent is generated by the rng() function, which multiplies three libc rand() values seeded from time(NULL). With approximately 31 bits of internal state and a time-based seed, the private exponent is recoverable in under a minute by a passive observer. A network attacker who can observe the MS-Logon II handshake (via sniffing, recording, or man-in-the-middle) can derive the shared DH key and decrypt the encapsulated username and password, resulting in full credential disclosure. This affects legacy MS-Logon II connections; MS-Logon III (X25519 + AES-256-GCM) is unaffected.

descriptions.description: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

cna.title: UltraVNC repeater authenticated out-of-bounds write in rule parser via oversized token

descriptions.value: UltraVNC repeater through 1.8.2.2 contains a post-authentication out-of-bounds write in the allow/deny rule parser. In repeater/webgui/settings.c:225-272, after strncpy_s copies a rule token into temp1[rule1] (25-byte destination) or temp2/temp3 (16-byte destination), the code unconditionally writes a NUL terminator at temp1[rule1][len] = 0 without clamping len to the destination size. When an authenticated administrator saves a rule with a token length equal to or greater than the destination size, the NUL byte is written one or more bytes past the end of the stack-allocated array, corrupting adjacent stack data. An attacker who has obtained admin credentials (including via CVE-2026-7839 default password) can trigger this to gain code execution on the repeater host.

cna.title: FormCraft <= 3.9.14 - Unauthenticated Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Matrix Field Sub-Parameters

descriptions.value: The FormCraft plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '[parameter name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.9.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit chain combines a server-side gap — where composite matrix sub-field keys such as field2_0 and field2_1 are never passed through the sanitization loop and are stored raw via $wpdb->insert() — with a client-side gap where DOMPurify is only invoked when typeof field.value === 'string', but matrix values arrive from the server as arrays, bypassing the check before being mapped to strings and injected into the DOM. Additionally, the same sink is reachable via a second attack vector: array-typed field values are passed through htmlentities() on submission but later reversed by html_entity_decode() at formcraft-main.php:2608 and :2122, restoring the malicious payload before storage and rendering.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

cna.title: UltraVNC viewer heap buffer overflow via integer overflow in RFB connection-failure reason length

timeline.value: Vulnerability discovered and crash-confirmed with AddressSanitizer

descriptions.value: UltraVNC viewer through 1.8.2.2 contains an integer overflow leading to a heap buffer overflow in the RFB protocol failure-response parsing path. In vncviewer/ClientConnection.cpp, the 4-byte network-supplied reasonLen field (type CARD32) is passed as reasonLen+1 to CheckBufferSize(). Because both operands are unsigned 32-bit, a reasonLen of 0xFFFFFFFF overflows to 0, causing CheckBufferSize to allocate only 256 bytes. The subsequent ReadString(m_netbuf, reasonLen) call then performs ReadExact for the original 4 GiB length into that 256-byte heap buffer. This overflow is reachable via rfbConnFailed (auth-scheme negotiation) and rfbVncAuthFailed (post-handshake) message types without successful authentication. A malicious VNC server, or any man-in-the-middle on the RFB stream, can trigger this condition when the victim viewer connects, potentially resulting in remote code execution as the user running the viewer. The crash was confirmed with AddressSanitizer on a portable reproduction harness (heap-buffer-overflow WRITE at offset 256).

descriptions.value: A session fixation vulnerability was found in Keycloak's login-actions endpoints. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this flaw by pre-creating an authentication session and tricking a victim into visiting a maliciously crafted link. By leveraging the /login-actions/restart endpoint—which processes session handles without adequate CSRF protection or cookie ownership validation—an attacker can reset the authentication flow state. This causes Single Sign-On (SSO) to authenticate the victim transparently upon clicking the link, allowing the attacker to hijack the required-action form without needing the victim's credentials. A successful exploit could lead to complete account takeover, including highly privileged administrative accounts.

cna.title: Concrete CMS 9.5.0 and below is vulnerable to CSRF via the DeleteFile controller

descriptions.value: CAPEC-122 Privilege Abuse

Concrete CMS  9.5.0 and below is vulnerable to unauthorized file deletion due to an Inverted CSRF token check in the DeleteFile controller. The code throws an error when the token IS valid and proceeds with file deletion when the token is invalid or missing. This effectively disables CSRF protection for the file deletion endpoint, allowing cross-site request forgery attacks against users who have permission to edit conversation messages. The Concrete CMS security team gave this vulnerability a CVSS v.4.0 score of 2.3 with a vector of CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. Thanks Tristan Mandani for reporting.

cna.title: Frontend User Notes <= 2.1.1 - Cross-Site Request Forgery to Note Content Modification via 'confirmEdit' Action

descriptions.value: The Frontend User Notes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.1. This is due to missing or incorrect nonce validation on the funp_ajax_modify_notes function. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to trick a logged-in user into visiting a malicious page, causing unauthorized overwriting of that victim's own note content via a forged cross-site request to wp_update_post() via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Due to ownership enforcement comparing the note's stored _funp_single_user_id meta against the current session's user ID, the attack is limited to modifying only notes belonging to the tricked victim, and cannot be used to alter notes owned by arbitrary third-party users.

cna.title: LearnPress – WordPress LMS Plugin for Create and Sell Online Courses <= 4.3.5 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Payment Bypass to Free Course Enrollment via 'quantity' Parameter

affected.product: LearnPress – WordPress LMS Plugin for Create and Sell Online Courses

descriptions.value: The LearnPress – WordPress LMS Plugin for Create and Sell Online Courses plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to payment bypass through user-controlled key in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.5. This is due to improper handling of user-supplied request parameters in the REST API endpoint, which passes the unsanitized parameter array to the add_to_cart() function where array_merge() allows attacker-controlled values to overwrite hardcoded defaults. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to enroll in any paid course entirely free of charge by supplying a quantity value of zero, which causes the order total to calculate as $0 and bypasses all payment gateway requirements.

descriptions.description: CWE-639 Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

cna.title: Simple History – Track, Log, and Audit WordPress Changes <= 5.26.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) Account Takeover via Missing Authorization on Event Reaction Endpoint

affected.product: Simple History – Track, Log, and Audit WordPress Changes

descriptions.value: The Simple History – Track, Log, and Audit WordPress Changes plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authenticated (Subscriber+) account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 5.26.0 via the event reaction endpoints (react_to_event() / unreact_to_event()). The endpoints register get_items_permissions_check() as their permission_callback, which only verifies the requester is logged in and does not enforce the per-logger capability checks normally applied by Log_Query. As a result, a Subscriber-level user can POST to /wp-json/simple-history/v1/events/<id>/react with the _fields=context query parameter and read the full context of any Simple History event — including SimpleUserLogger entries that record the full password-reset email body (reset URL with the reset key) for any user. The attacker triggers a password reset for an administrator via the lost-password form, brute-forces recent event IDs through the reaction endpoint to read the resulting user_requested_password_reset_link event, extracts the reset key from context.message, and completes the password reset to take over the administrator account. Exploitation requires an administrator to have first enabled the experimental features option (simple_history_experimental_features_enabled), which is not the default.

descriptions.description: CWE-640 Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

cna.title: Click to Chat <= 4.39 - Authenticated (Contributor+) Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'num' Shortcode Parameter

descriptions.value: The Click to Chat – WA Widget plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the [chat] shortcode 'num' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.38. This is due to insufficient escaping when embedding user-supplied shortcode attribute values inside JavaScript string literals that are then placed in HTML event-handler attributes. The CCW_Shortcode::shortcode() function applies esc_attr() to the 'num' parameter (line 157), which converts single quotes to the HTML entity '. This entity-encoded value is then interpolated directly into a JavaScript window.open() call string delimited by single quotes (line 194/221), and that complete string is placed verbatim into an HTML onclick attribute in the style template files (e.g., sc-style-1.php line 6). Because browsers HTML-decode event attribute values before executing the embedded JavaScript, the ' entities are decoded back to literal single quotes at runtime, allowing the injected payload to break out of the JavaScript string context and execute arbitrary code. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers with Contributor-level access and above to inject arbitrary web scripts into pages that will execute whenever a user clicks the WhatsApp chat button rendered by the [chat] shortcode.

descriptions.description: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

cna.title: Out-of-Bounds Write via Unsanitized Prefix Length in Router Advertisement Processing in FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP

descriptions.value: CAPEC-153: Input Data Manipulation

Insufficient validation of the prefix length field in IPv6 Router Advertisement processing in FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP before V4.2.6 and V4.4.1 allows an adjacent network actor to cause memory corruption by sending a crafted Router Advertisement with a prefix length value exceeding the maximum valid length, resulting in a heap buffer overflow. Users processing IPv4 RA only are not impacted.



To mitigate this issue, users should upgrade to the fixed version when available.
