cna.title: tcp: ipv6: clamp default adverting MSS to avoid GSO_BY_FRAGS (0xFFFF)

scenarios.value:
AV:N - Reachable from the network via IPv6 TCP: a remote peer sends a crafted SYN (MSS=65535) or connects over a large-MTU IPv6 route, causing outbound TCP GSO skbs with gso_size=0xFFFF to be software-segmented in skb_segment() during normal packet transmit.
AC:L - The attacker controls the TCP handshake MSS option and can induce >64KB outbound segments; syzbot reproduced this reliably, and software GSO paths (loopback, veth, NETIF_F_GSO_SOFTWARE) are common in cloud/container deployments where skb_segment() is invoked.
PR:N - No privileges are required; exploitation occurs on the pre-authentication passive-open path where the kernel accepts a remote TCP SYN and MSS option before any application-level authentication.
UI:N - No victim user interaction is needed beyond the target system normally accepting IPv6 TCP connections and transmitting response data to the attacker-controlled peer.
S:U - The vulnerability causes a kernel crash on the attacked host itself; it does not cross a security boundary such as a VM escape, container sandbox breakout, or IOMMU/DMA isolation bypass.
C:N - Impact is a NULL pointer dereference in skb_segment() when gso_size equals GSO_BY_FRAGS; there is no out-of-bounds read, use-after-free, or other memory disclosure primitive.
I:N - The bug does not corrupt or modify attacker-controlled memory; it dereferences a NULL frag_list pointer during segmentation, yielding a crash rather than a write or code-execution primitive.
A:H - The NULL pointer dereference in skb_segment() triggers a kernel oops/panic, causing complete loss of availability for the affected system when the malicious IPv6 TCP traffic path is exercised.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tcp: ipv6: clamp default adverting MSS to avoid GSO_BY_FRAGS (0xFFFF)

When MTU is large, ip6_default_advmss() can return IPV6_MAXPLEN (65535).
This is interpreted by TCP as mss_clamp, allowing the MSS to reach 65535.

However, 0xFFFF is also used as a magic value GSO_BY_FRAGS in the kernel.
If a TCP packet with gso_size=0xFFFF is passed to skb_segment(), it will
be mistakenly treated as GSO_BY_FRAGS, leading to a NULL pointer
dereference because local TCP packets do not use frag_list.

Fix this by returning min(IPV6_MAXPLEN, GSO_BY_FRAGS - 1) (65534) from
ip6_default_advmss() when MTU is large.

Also update the stale comment in ip6_default_advmss() which suggested
that IPV6_MAXPLEN is returned to mean "any MSS".

cna.title: selinux: check connect-related permissions on TCP Fast Open

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Exploitation requires a confined local process to invoke sendmsg(2)/sendto(2) with MSG_FASTOPEN; the vulnerable selinux_socket_sendmsg() LSM hook runs on the syscall path before TCP fast-open performs its implicit connect.
AC:L - A confined task with SOCKET__WRITE can reliably trigger the bypass with one sendmsg/sendto using MSG_FASTOPEN and a destination address; TFO client is enabled by default (sysctl_tcp_fastopen=TFO_CLIENT_ENABLE) and no race or special victim state is needed.
PR:L - The attacker must be an unprivileged process in a SELinux domain that grants socket write but denies connect/name_connect (e.g., confined Android apps, container workloads, hardened service domains); no real root or init-namespace privileges are required.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required; the confined attacker process directly issues the bypassing syscall without needing another user or administrator to perform any action.
S:C - Successful exploitation crosses the SELinux MAC confinement boundary, allowing a sandboxed domain to establish outbound TCP/MPTCP connections that connect(2) and name_connect policy would have blocked, escaping the intended network policy scope.
C:H - Bypassing connect and name_connect mediation lets a confined process open TCP/MPTCP sessions to SELinux-forbidden destinations and read arbitrary response data from those services (internal APIs, metadata endpoints, databases), constituting unauthorized information disclosure.
I:H - The bypass enables unauthorized outbound connection establishment and transmission of arbitrary application data (including SYN-cookie payload) to hosts and ports explicitly denied by SELinux connect/name_connect rules, violating integrity of the confinement policy.
A:N - This is a pure SELinux LSM policy-bypass flaw with no kernel memory corruption, panic, oops, hang, or resource exhaustion; exploitation does not impact system availability.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

selinux: check connect-related permissions on TCP Fast Open

Similar to Landlock, SELinux was not updated when TCP Fast Open
support was introduced to ensure connect-related permissions are
checked when using TCP Fast Open. Update its socket_sendmsg() hook to
call selinux_socket_connect() when MSG_FASTOPEN is passed.

cna.title: Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader vulnerable to denial of service via YAML alias expansion

descriptions.value: The OpenAPI.NET SDK contains a useful object model for OpenAPI documents in .NET along with common serializers to extract raw OpenAPI JSON and YAML documents from the model. In Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers versions before 1.6.30 and Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader from 2.0.0-preview.11 through 2.11.0 and 3.0.0 through 3.9.0, parsing a YAML OpenAPI document with nested anchors and aliases can consume uncontrolled memory. SharpYaml represents aliases as shared nodes in a small directed acyclic graph, but conversion to independent OpenAPI or System.Text.Json.Nodes.JsonNode trees duplicates every aliased path; without a node-count or nesting-depth limit, N nested anchors referenced k times can require k^N materialized nodes and terminate the process through an out-of-memory condition. The fixed readers bound materialization to 5,000,000 nodes and a nesting depth of 64 by default and report an OpenApiDiagnostic error when a limit is exceeded. This vulnerability is fixed in Microsoft.OpenApi.Readers 1.6.30 and Microsoft.OpenApi.YamlReader 2.12.0 and 3.10.0.

cna.title: AnythingLLM: Password recovery accepts one recovery code twice after whitespace normalization

descriptions.value: AnythingLLM is an application that turns pieces of content into context that any LLM can use as references during chatting. From 1.0.0 to 1.15.0, AnythingLLM's unauthenticated account-recovery flow in server/utils/PasswordRecovery/index.js uses recoverAccount() to deduplicate the raw recoveryCodes values before trimming them, so one valid code submitted twice with different surrounding whitespace can satisfy the two-code check. cna.title: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value in Elasticsearch Leading to Denial of Service

The resulting out-of-memory condition is fatal and terminates the affected node process, resulting in a denial of service.

cna.title: netfilter: xt_connmark: reject invalid shift parameters

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Malformed CONNMARK rev2 rules are installed via IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt or nftables NFNetlink (nft_compat); per kernel CNA guidance netfilter/xtables rule setup is Local even though installed rules later evaluate on ingress/egress packets through ipt_do_table/ip6t_do_table.
AC:L - The attacker fully controls shift_bits and shift_dir in xt_connmark_tginfo2 when installing the rev2 CONNMARK target and can send conntrack-tracked packets to reliably hit connmark_tg_shift(); no race, memory layout, or victim state outside attacker control is required.
PR:L - Installing CONNMARK iptables/nftables rules requires CAP_NET_ADMIN in the target network namespace, obtainable by unprivileged users via unshare -Urn; ip_tables.c do_ipt_set_ctl() and nfnetlink.c nfnetlink_rcv() enforce ns_capable/netlink_net_capable against the namespace user_ns.
UI:N - The attacker installs the malformed CONNMARK rev2 rule and generates matching conntrack-associated traffic in their namespace; no separate victim action such as opening files, mounting media, or clicking links is required.
S:U - Undefined shift during xt_CONNMARK packet targeting and resulting mark corruption remain within the host kernel security authority; this is standard local kernel netfilter compromise, not a VM escape, IOMMU bypass, or sandbox boundary crossing.
C:L - Undefined-behavior shifts on 32-bit mark values produce attacker-influenced unpredictable ct->mark and skb->mark results observable through conntrack netlink and mark-based iptables/nftables matches, leaking altered connection-classification state within the namespace.
I:H - Invalid shift_bits or shift_dir corrupt connmark_tg_shift() output written to nf_conn->mark and skb->mark, subverting mark-dependent firewall, policy-routing, QoS, and multi-tenant container egress controls on cloud routers and internet-facing servers.
A:H - Evaluating a malformed CONNMARK rev2 rule with shift_bits>=32 triggers C11 undefined-shift UB in connmark_tg_shift() during softirq netfilter processing; UBSAN-instrumented kernels panic on shift-out-of-bounds, and UB in the packet hot path can destabilize conntrack-driven forwarding.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

netfilter: xt_connmark: reject invalid shift parameters

Revision 2 of the CONNMARK target accepts user-controlled shift
parameters and applies them to 32-bit mark values in
connmark_tg_shift().

A shift_bits value of 32 or more triggers an undefined-shift bug when
the rule is evaluated. Invalid shift_dir values are also accepted and
silently fall back to the left-shift path.

Reject invalid revision-2 shift parameters in connmark_tg_check() so
malformed rules fail at installation time, before they can reach the
packet path.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: xen: scsiback: Free unsubmitted command instead of double-putting it

scsiback_get_pend_req() obtains a command tag and returns a vscsibk_pend
whose embedded se_cmd has only been memset to 0, so its cmd_kref is 0;
the se_cmd is initialised (kref_init() via target_init_cmd()) only
later, in scsiback_cmd_exec(), on the successful VSCSIIF_ACT_SCSI_CDB
path. The two error paths in scsiback_do_cmd_fn() taken before the
command is submitted -- a failed scsiback_gnttab_data_map() and an
unknown ring_req.act -- call
transport_generic_free_cmd(&pending_req->se_cmd, 0), which kref_put()s a
refcount of 0. That underflows it ("refcount_t: underflow;
use-after-free") and, as the release function is not run, leaks the
command tag.

Impact: a pvSCSI guest can leak every command tag of a LUN's session,
stopping the LUN, by submitting requests with a bad grant reference or
an unknown request type; under panic_on_warn the refcount underflow
panics the host.

Add a helper that just returns the tag with target_free_tag() and sends
the error response. It frees the tag while the v2p reference still pins
the session, and snapshots the response fields beforehand because
freeing the tag can let another ring reuse the pending_req slot.

scenarios.value:
AV:L - A malicious Xen pvSCSI guest reaches scsiback_do_cmd_fn() by posting vscsiif_request entries on the shared ring and notifying the dom0/driver-domain backend via event channel; this is a hypervisor-mediated local interface, not a routable network or physical bus path.
AC:L - The guest fully controls ring_req.act and grant references and can deterministically trigger the two pre-submit error paths (unknown act or failed scsiback_gnttab_data_map) on every attempt with no race, timing window, or other condition outside attacker control.
PR:N - Exploitation requires only a compromised or malicious Xen guest that has been granted a pvSCSI device with a mapped LUN; no dom0 account, capability, or init-namespace privilege is needed—only tenant VM control in the standard Xen multi-tenant threat model.
UI:N - The guest frontend posts crafted pvSCSI ring requests autonomously; no victim user action on dom0 such as mounting storage, opening device nodes, or approving prompts is required beyond routine PV device assignment already present.
S:C - A guest VM drives vulnerable code in the dom0/driver-domain xen-scsiback backend kernel, crossing the VM/host security boundary and impacting host kernel state, storage availability, and potentially the entire physical host.
C:H - The buggy error paths call transport_generic_free_cmd() on an uninitialized se_cmd whose cmd_kref is zero, causing refcount underflow with kernel "use-after-free" warnings; per kernel CNA guidance, refcount/UAF-class defects warrant High confidentiality impact.
I:H - Refcount underflow corrupts cmd_kref without invoking the proper release path, leaving target-core command state inconsistent; per kernel CNA guidance for UAF/refcount memory-safety bugs, this warrants High integrity impact even if primary observed effect is tag leak.
A:H - Each trigger leaks one session command tag from the finite per-LUN pool (default 128), and exhausting all tags permanently stops the LUN; on hosts with panic_on_warn enabled the refcount underflow WARN additionally panics the host kernel.

cna.title: soundwire: fix bug in sdw_add_element_group_count found by syzkaller

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Vulnerable sdw_add_element_group_count is reached only via local ALSA PCM ioctl (SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_PREPARE/HW_PARAMS) on /dev/snd/pcmC*D*, through asoc_sdw_prepare -> sdw_prepare_stream -> sdw_compute_params on Intel SoundWire machines; no network or adjacent-network entry point exists.
AC:L - The off-by-one loop (i <= num when num==group->count) deterministically reads one slot past the rates/lanes arrays whenever a second distinct rate/lane group entry is added, which an attacker can trigger by preparing SoundWire streams that exercise multilane assignment or multiple active bus runtimes without races or external state.
PR:L - Exploitation requires only the ability to open and ioctl the ALSA PCM character device (typically granted to unprivileged desktop users via the audio group or logind seat ACLs on Intel SOF/SoundWire laptops); no CAP_SYS_ADMIN, real root, or non-namespace capability is checked on this path.
UI:N - The attacker's own process issues the PCM prepare/hw_params ioctls that drive bandwidth recomputation; no separate victim must mount filesystems, open files, or take any other action beyond the attacker already having local device access.
S:U - The out-of-bounds access corrupts/read kernel heap memory within the SoundWire bandwidth allocator in the same kernel security domain; it does not cross VM, container, IOMMU, or sandbox boundaries.
C:H - When i==group->count the loop compares against group->rates[i] and group->lanes[i] one element beyond the allocated arrays, leaking adjacent kmalloc heap contents; per kernel guidance unbounded out-of-bounds reads in the allocator path warrant High confidentiality impact.
I:H - Even though the immediate fault is an OOB read, the same loop guards heap-backed dynamic expansion that then writes attacker-influenced rate/lane tuples into rates[]/lanes[]; adjacent-heap corruption from the read plus controlled follow-on writes is leverageable for integrity compromise consistent with similar SoundWire CVE scoring.
A:H - The out-of-bounds read can fault on unmapped adjacent slab memory or trip KASAN/hardened checks (as syzkaller reported), producing kernel oops/panic and aborting stream prepare, leaving audio/DSP subsystems unavailable on affected Intel SoundWire platforms.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

soundwire: fix bug in sdw_add_element_group_count found by syzkaller

The original implementation caused an out-of-bounds memory access
in the sdw_add_element_group_count for-loop when i == num.

for (i = 0; i <= num; i++) {
    if (rate == group->rates[i] && lane == group->lanes[i])
        ...

To fix this error, the function now checks for existing rate/lane
entries in the group(a function parameter) using a for-loop before
adding them.

No functional changes apart from this fix.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

cna.title: md/raid1: fix writes_pending and barrier reference leaks on write failures

scenarios.value:
AV:N - The bug is in md/raid1 write handling reached via block-layer writes to RAID1-backed volumes; on storage servers and appliances, remote NFS, SMB (ksmbd), iSCSI, and NVMe-oF clients submit those writes through md_submit_bio() to raid1_make_request() the same as local I/O.
AC:L - An attacker with write access can reliably trigger the leaks using RWF_NOWAIT during active resync/barriers, against mirrors in BlockedBadBlocks state after prior write errors, or via bio_submit_split_bioset() failure paths; they control I/O timing and concurrency without uncontrollable races.
PR:L - Exploitation requires only the ability to issue writes to the RAID1 array—via a mounted filesystem, O_RDWR on /dev/mdX, or an authenticated network storage client—not CAP_SYS_ADMIN or other privileges needed to create or reconfigure the md array.
UI:N - No victim interaction is required; the attacker or their storage client issues the triggering RWF_NOWAIT or failing write requests directly, with no separate mount, file open, or administrator action needed at exploitation time.
S:U - Impact is confined to kernel md RAID1 write/barrier accounting and array lifecycle state within the same host kernel; it does not cross VM, container, or IOMMU security boundaries.
C:N - Leaked writes_pending and nr_pending reference counters do not corrupt memory, read out of bounds, or use-after-free; there is no kernel pointer leak or arbitrary memory disclosure primitive.
I:L - Skipped md_write_end() on failure paths leaves writes_pending inflated and prevents set_in_sync()/clean sysfs transitions, causing persistent incorrect RAID1 dirty/clean metadata state that cannot be corrected until reboot.
A:H - Leaked conf->nr_pending from the wait_blocked_rdev()+REQ_NOWAIT path inflates get_unqueued_pending() so freeze_array() wait_event never completes, deadlocking array quiesce, reshape, removal, and read-error recovery while array_frozen blocks new I/O.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

md/raid1: fix writes_pending and barrier reference leaks on write failures

raid1_make_request() acquires a writes_pending reference with
md_write_start() before calling raid1_write_request(). Several failure
paths in raid1_write_request() complete the bio and return without
reaching the normal write completion path, causing the corresponding
md_write_end() to be skipped.

Make raid1_write_request() return a status indicating whether the write
request was successfully queued. This allows raid1_make_request() to
call md_write_end() when raid1_write_request() fails.

Additionally, if wait_blocked_rdev() fails after wait_barrier()
succeeds, the associated barrier reference is not released.

Call allow_barrier() before returning from that path to keep the barrier
accounting balanced.

cna.title: bridge: stp: Fix a potential use-after-free when deleting a bridge

scenarios.value:
AV:L - Exploitation is via local RTNETLINK/ioctl to create a down bridge, enable kernel STP, enslave ports, and delete the bridge; remote STP BPDU handling is blocked when IFF_UP is clear, so the arming path that leaves timers active on a down bridge is local.
AC:L - The public PoC uses a reliable, attacker-controlled netlink sequence (down bridge + kernel STP + port state progression + dellink) without winning races; per-port forward-delay timers deterministically reach br_topology_change_detection and arm topology_change_timer before deletion.
PR:L - All reachable paths (RTM_NEWLINK/DELLINK, IFLA_BR_STP_STATE, enslaving ports) require CAP_NET_ADMIN, which unprivileged users can obtain in user/network namespaces (unshare -Urn, Kubernetes NET_ADMIN, LXC/libvirt network namespaces).
UI:N - Triggering requires only programmatic bridge configuration by the attacker; no victim must click, mount, or open anything beyond the attacker's own netlink operations.
S:U - Impact is kernel memory corruption and privilege escalation within the same kernel/host security domain; it does not cross a VM, container-to-host, or IOMMU boundary by itself.
C:H - Use-after-free of the net_device/net_bridge kmalloc object lets an attacker reclaim freed slab memory and obtain arbitrary kernel read/disclosure primitives from corrupted timer and bridge structures.
I:H - Disclosed analysis and PoC show the dangling timer callback can hijack control flow by reclaiming the freed object with attacker-controlled data, replacing the timer function pointer for arbitrary kernel code execution.
A:H - Deleting the bridge with active STP timers queued causes the per-CPU timer wheel to invoke callbacks on freed memory, producing kernel BUG/oops/panics and denial of service even if full exploitation is not attempted.

descriptions.value:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

bridge: stp: Fix a potential use-after-free when deleting a bridge

The three STP timers are not supposed to be armed while the bridge is
administratively down. They are synchronously deactivated when the
bridge is put administratively down and the various call sites check for
'IFF_UP' before arming them.

This check is missing from br_topology_change_detection() and it is
possible to engineer a situation in which the topology change timer is
armed while the bridge is administratively down, resulting in a
use-after-free [1] when the bridge is deleted.

Fix by adding the missing check and for good measures synchronously
shutdown the three timers when the bridge is deleted.

[1]
ODEBUG: free active (active state 0) object: ffff88811662b9b0 object type: timer_list hint: br_topology_change_timer_expired (net/bridge/br_stp_timer.c:120)
WARNING: lib/debugobjects.c:629 at debug_print_object+0x1bc/0x450, CPU#9: ip/359

From 17.0.0 until 21.0.4, packages/happy-dom/src/module/ECMAScriptModuleCompiler.ts accepts a named ESM import alias without validating that it is a JavaScript binding identifier before inserting it into a generated destructuring binding. With enableJavaScriptEvaluation enabled, attacker-controlled HTML or module source can use an invalid alias that becomes a valid default initializer after compilation, causing the generated JavaScript to execute in the Node.js host process. cna.title: Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regular expression backtracking when decoding chunked request bodies

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starlet 0.33 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starlet versions from 0.20 before 0.33 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via regular expression backtracking when decoding chunked request bodies.

A chunk-size line is matched as a run of hex digits, then .* and a CRLF. A run followed by a bare LF and then a CRLF can never match, and the engine retries the match once for each digit, so the time taken grows with the square of the run length. Nothing limits the length of the run, which can span several reads.

A remote attacker can occupy a worker for about a minute of CPU time with one 128 KiB request, before the application is called.

cna.title: WP STAGING <= 4.19.0 - Authenticated (Administrator+) Arbitrary Directory Deletion via 'deleteDir' Parameter

affected.product: WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups

descriptions.value: The WP STAGING – Backups & Restore, Migration & Clone Plugin – Cloud Backups, Scheduled Backups plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary Directory Deletion in all versions up to, and including, 4.19.0. This is due to insufficient path validation in the `cleanStagingDirectory` function, where the `deleteDir` parameter is only stripped of whitespace and double slashes by `sanitizePath()` without removing `..` traversal sequences or enforcing containment within the staging directory, leaving the sole pre-deletion guard as a simple string equality check against the WordPress home path. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with administrator-level access and above, to recursively delete arbitrary directories on the server — including `wp-content`, `wp-admin`, or directories outside the WordPress installation on shared hosting — resulting in denial of service or permanent data loss. An attacker must sequence a clone start, cancellation, and restart to drive the `delete_job` cache into the `directory` step before re-cancelling with a manipulated `deleteDir` value supplied via the `wp_ajax_wpstg_cancel_clone` endpoint.

descriptions.value: The Libreswan IKEv2 state machine did not verify that an IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange was required to satisfy the addke= PostQuantum algorithm component of the exchange. A connecting client could (maliciously or by implementation error) skip the IKE_INTERMEDIATE exchange and start an IKE_AUTH exchange prematurely. The result is as if the addke= option had not been specified, and such connections are only protected by the classic key exchange algorithm (such as P-256 or Curve25519), allowing "store now, decrypt later" attacks once a quantum computer becomes available. Only connections with the addke= keyword in the ike= and/or esp= configuration option are affected. PostQuantum Hybrid Key Exchange support was added in version 5.4.

descriptions.value:
Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in hackney_ssl in benoitc hackney allows an on-path attacker to impersonate a server pinned to a private certificate authority via a certificate chain that ends in a publicly trusted root. hackney adds {partial_chain, fun hackney_ssl:partial_chain/1} to every verify_peer configuration. The callback returns any certificate in the peer chain whose public key matches a root in the bundled certifi store as the trust anchor, and OTP honours that callback over the configured cacerts. hackney_ssl:merge_ssl_opts/3 kept the callback when the caller replaced the trust store with cacerts or cacertfile in ssl_options, so a connection pinned to a private CA still accepted any chain that carried a publicly trusted root.

The hostname check still applies, so the attacker needs a publicly trusted certificate for the pinned hostname.

This issue affects hackney: from 1.24.0 before 4.9.0.

1. Default trust options. hackney_ssl:check_hostname_opts/1 builds the verify_peer options for every TLS connection: the certifi cacerts, a hostname verify_fun, and {partial_chain, fun hackney_ssl:partial_chain/1}. The callback walks the peer chain and returns {trusted_ca, Cert} for the first certificate whose public key matches a root in the bundled certifi store, which lets OTP accept chains that end in a cross-signed root.

2. Merge keeps the callback. When the caller passes ssl_options, hackney_ssl:merge_ssl_opts/3 merges them over the defaults with the caller's values winning per key. cacerts or cacertfile replace the trust store, and a cacertfile removes the default cacerts, but partial_chain has no counterpart in the caller's options and stays.

3. Validation. OTP consults partial_chain before the configured trust store. A peer chain that carries any publicly trusted root therefore gets that root as its trust anchor, and the pinned cacerts are never consulted. Only the hostname verify_fun still constrains the attacker.

descriptions.value:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in ash-project ash_postgres allows a user to read another tenant's record through a skipped upsert.

When Ash.bulk_create/4 or a single create runs as an upsert with return_skipped_upsert?: true and the upsert is skipped (for example because its upsert_condition does not hold), AshPostgres.DataLayer reads the existing row back by the upsert identity in do_bulk_create/3 and upsert/4. That lookup did not apply the resource's attribute multitenancy, so on a resource using strategy :attribute it could match and return the row of another tenant with the same identity values, exposing its fields to the caller.

This issue affects ash_postgres: from 2.6.22 before 2.15.2.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in the HTTP/2 request body reader of mtrudel bandit allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to hold stream processes open indefinitely via WINDOW_UPDATE or empty SETTINGS frames sent while a Plug reads the request body.

Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.do_read_data/4 in lib/bandit/http2/stream.ex waits for each frame with a fresh read_timeout. A stream WINDOW_UPDATE, or the zero-delta window update that every empty SETTINGS frame delivers to all streams, ends the wait without delivering any body data, and the loop starts a new full countdown. A client that sends one of these 9-byte frames before each countdown expires keeps read_body blocked, together with the stream process and whatever the application holds while reading, for as long as it likes.

This issue affects bandit: from 1.4.0 before 1.14.0.

x_technicalAnalysis.value:
1. Per-receive timeout. Bandit.HTTP2.Stream.read_data/2 passes a flat read_timeout (default 15,000 ms) to do_read_data/4, which blocks in do_recv/2's receive ... after timeout.

2. Non-progress frames end the wait. A stream WINDOW_UPDATE, delivered through Bandit.HTTP2.Connection.handle_frame/3, or an empty SETTINGS frame, which delivers a zero-delta window update to every stream, is matched inside that receive. do_recv_send_window_update/2 returns a bare %Stream{}, and do_read_data/4 recurses with the identical timeout, restarting the countdown.

3. Nothing else bounds the read. The transport read timeout fires only when no bytes arrive, max_bytes is decremented only by DATA frames, and neither WINDOW_UPDATE nor SETTINGS frames are rate limited. The send path in do_send_data/4 uses a progress-based deadline; the read path does not.

cna.title: Arbitrary file read and backend crash through unrestricted provider method calls

descriptions.value: Any registered user can read any file the backend process can read, with the result returned as bytes so binary files work.

The backend's environment is readable, which exposes the JWT signing secret, the database and Redis connection strings and the credentials and API keys of connected providers when they are passed as environment variables.

With the JWT signing secret an attacker can sign a session for any user, including a user in another organization or an instance super administrator, and can decrypt data the application stores encrypted with the same secret.
A single request ends the backend process, and it can be repeated after every restart.
Other provider functions become callable by any member of an organization that owns a channel, some of which return access tokens for the connected account that other routes keep server side.

exploits.value: Exploitation was demonstrated end to end against an unmodified build of Postiz at commit 3a7d28b7ad96, using only a self-registered account: the contents of a file placed outside the application's directories and the exact JWT secret the backend was started with were both returned in full. Terminating the backend with one request was demonstrated separately.

timeline.value: Anthropic has disclosed a thorough report of this vulnerability including a working PoC to Postiz
Postiz has reproduced the vulnerability and is working on a fix
Postiz has pushed a fix for this vulnerability and verified it
Postiz has created a release and published the advisory

workarounds.value: Set DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. The attacker needs an ordinary account, so closing self-registration limits exposure to people who already hold one. This reduces reach, it does not close the issue.

descriptions.value:
Postiz lets a signed-in user ask the backend to run a function on one of their connected channels. The backend did not restrict which functions can be requested, so a user could call internal helper functions that were never meant to be reachable from the web interface.

One of those helpers reads a file from the server's disk. A user who connects a channel whose stored token is a file path can have the backend return the contents of any file it can read, including its environment, which holds the secret used to sign login sessions, the database address and the credentials of connected services. Another helper makes the backend process exit with a single request. Self-registration is open by default, so no existing account and no action by another user is needed.

configurations.value: The default configuration is affected and no setting has to be changed. Self-registration is open unless DISABLE_REGISTRATION is set to true; with registration closed, any existing user can still exploit the issue.
The image built from the project's Dockerfile.dev runs the process as root, so every file root can read is exposed. The process's own environment is readable regardless of the user it runs as.

descriptions.value:
Interpretation Conflict vulnerability in hackney_url in benoitc hackney allows Server Side Request Forgery via a percent-encoded bracketed IPv6 literal or an IP literal with a trailing dot. A host such as %5B%3A%3Affff%3A127%2E0%2E0%2E1%5D (decoding to [::ffff:127.0.0.1]) or 127.0.0.1. is not an IP address to a caller's allowlist built on uri_string:parse/1 and inet:parse_address/1, while hackney connects to the address it denotes. The same applies to a Location target when redirects are followed.

The IP-literal gate that hackney_url:normalize/2 applies to a percent-decoded host, added to close the percent-encoded IP bypass of CVE-2026-47076, passes the decoded value to inet_parse:address/1 as is. The connect path in hackney_happy:parse_address/1 drops a surrounding bracket pair, and the resolver ignores a trailing dot, so both forms pass the gate and still reach the literal address. Domain names with a trailing dot and unencoded IPv6 literals are not affected.

This issue affects hackney: from 4.0.1 before 4.9.0.

cna.title: Prevent shadowing stdlib in gzip/tarfile/zipfile CLI during extraction

descriptions.value:
When tarfile or zipfile command line interface (CLI) is used to

decompress an archive, a Python script shadowing the stdlib can be

created. Then if an error occurs during decompressing the next file,

the newly created Python script is executed. This is especially true

if the created Python is called traceback.py. The problem is that

Python adds the current directory to sys.path when python -m MODULE is

run, and the archive is also decompressed in the current directory.



The fix removes sys.path[0] in gzip, tarfile and zipfile command line

interface to prevent shadowing standard library modules from extracted

files.

descriptions.value: External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter (CWE-472) in the cart and checkout flow of MarcosCamara01 Ecommerce Template allows an authenticated user with no special privileges to be charged the price of one product while placing an order for another, because POST /api/user/cart accepts variantId, which determines what the order records, and stripeId, which determines what Stripe charges, as two independent fields of the request body, stores both on the cart row, and no check requires the stripeId to be the one that belongs to the variantId. cna.title: obsidian-tc: Memory-lifecycle tools overwrite unowned notes or partially commit lifecycle changes

descriptions.value: obsidian-tc is a governed, agent-ready Model Context Protocol server for Obsidian vaults. From 1.0.1 until 1.31.4, `create_entity`, `link_entities`, `rename_entity`, `unlink_entities` and `delete_entity` regenerate memory notes from SQLite at the computed `memory/<type>/<name>.md` path without reliably preserving note ownership or the consistency of a failed lifecycle operation. During shared materialization, a hand-authored note or an orphan left by a different entity whose name sanitized to the same path could have its entire body overwritten on the next write naming that type and name, with non-owned frontmatter preserved. `rename_entity` also seeded the destination path with a direct atomic write without validating ownership and could overwrite a foreign note there. Separately, several tools mutated SQLite before fallible filesystem work: `create_entity` and `link_entities` inserted the row or relation before materialization; `rename_entity` updated the entity, including a retired status, before updating its note; `unlink_entities` removed a relation before rematerializing the source note; and `delete_entity`'s cascade removed the target and its relations before rematerializing neighbouring notes. A later filesystem failure could therefore leave a row or relation changed and the memory graph inconsistent with the notes on disk even when the operation failed. An authorized caller with the required memory-tool permissions could, without intending to, destroy the body of a vault note outside the entity being written; `delete_entity` additionally requires its deletion permission and destructive confirmation, which this memory flaw does not bypass. Snapshots-before-write through `restore_note` mitigate the overwrite only where snapshots are enabled and the note had previously been written through obsidian-tc. This issue is fixed in version 1.31.4.

cna.title: Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starlet 0.33 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starlet versions before 0.33 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory.

The request body is read in a loop that asks sysread for all of the remaining declared length at once. Perl grows the read buffer to that size before any data arrives, so a length larger than available memory makes the worker exit with an uncatchable out of memory error before the application is called.

A remote attacker can force a worker restart with each request of a few bytes.

descriptions.description: CWE-789 Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

cna.title: Twisted: Unauthenticated Remote Denial of Service in the Twisted conch Telnet Transport via an Unbounded Subnegotiation Buffer

descriptions.value: Twisted is an event-based framework for internet applications, supporting Python 3.6+. Prior to 26.10.0rc1, twisted.conch.telnet.Telnet.dataReceived appends every byte received after IAC SB to a persistent subnegotiation buffer until IAC SE is received, without applying a maximum length. Telnet option negotiation occurs before authentication, so an unauthenticated peer can omit the terminator and continuously grow the buffer. The resulting memory exhaustion can terminate the process and every service it hosts. This issue is fixed in version 26.10.0rc1.

cna.title: FreeSWITCH: Stack buffer overflow parsing the SDP a=crypto key material on inbound calls

descriptions.value: FreeSWITCH is a Software Defined Telecom Stack enabling the digital transformation from proprietary telecom switches to a software implementation that runs on any commodity hardware. Prior to 1.11.2, switch_core_media_add_crypto() passed the encoded key and salt length from an inbound SDP a=crypto attribute to switch_b64_decode() as the destination capacity. A zero-length key and salt made that capacity underflow, allowing the decoded attribute to overflow a fixed stack buffer with sender-chosen bytes before the call was answered. On the shipped external profile, an unauthenticated caller can reach the SDES-SRTP parser, while profiles that challenge inbound calls remain affected for senders who can authenticate; setting rtp_secure_media_inbound to false removes the path, and WebRTC DTLS-SRTP legs are unaffected. The overflow corrupts memory and can crash the FreeSWITCH process, dropping every active call, although remote code execution has not been demonstrated. This issue is fixed in version 1.11.2.

cna.title: baserCMS: Public Web API mail-form submission bypasses image CAPTCHA

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. In versions 5.0.0 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, the public POST /baser/api/bc-mail/mail_messages/add/{mailContentId}.json endpoint accepts submissions without enforcing the form's auth_captcha setting. BcMail\Controller\Api\MailMessagesController::add() and MailMessagesService::create() omit the BcCaptchaService::check() verification of captcha_id and auth_captcha performed by MailController::submit() in the web UI. An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the API can therefore automate submissions without solving the enabled image challenge. The API disables FormProtection and has no rate limit; submissions can generate administrator-inbox spam, send attacker-influenced auto-replies to third parties when an email field is present, and accumulate mail_messages database records when save_info is enabled. The API already enforces the isAccepting() check added for CVE-2026-30878; the missing CAPTCHA check is a separate control failure. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

cna.title: Improper Certificate Validation in Elastic Docker Images Leading to Interception of TLS Connections

descriptions.value: CAPEC-474 Signature Spoofing by Key Theft

Improper Certificate Validation (CWE-295) in the operating system certificate bundle shipped in the Docker images of APM Server; Auditbeat, Filebeat, Heartbeat, Metricbeat and Packetbeat; Elastic Agent, including Fleet Server and Cloudbeat; Logstash, for TLS connections that use the operating system certificate bundle; Elastic connectors; Universal Profiling (host agent, collector and symbolizer); and Elastic Maps Server. This certificate bundle, a dependency of these products (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to intercept or modify TLS-protected traffic via Signature Spoofing by Key Theft (CAPEC-474). The certificate bundle includes root certificate authorities that signed eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities whose private keys are compromised. Anyone with these keys can issue a certificate for any host name that these products accept as trusted. Exploitation requires an attacker in a network position between the product and the remote party, who presents a certificate issued with one of the compromised keys.

cna.title: User-mode module can post forged callback requests to another module's callback queue, running its code with that module's privilege

descriptions.value: In Eclipse ThreadX versions 6.0.1 through 6.5.2.202603, the Module Manager lets a user-mode, memory-protected module post a forged callback request to another module's callback request queue. The receiving module's callback thread calls the function pointer in the request without checking that the Module Manager sent it, so the attacker's code runs with the receiving module's privilege; when that module runs in privileged mode, a user-mode module gains privileged execution.

descriptions.value: A server-side template injection vulnerability exists in the Twig theme rendering sandbox of Mautic. The sandbox introduced to restrict user-uploaded theme templates (the fix for GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg) does not fully enforce its restrictions, allowing a crafted theme template to escape the sandbox. An authenticated user with the core:themes:create permission can upload a malicious theme whose template is later rendered, resulting in execution of arbitrary code on the server with the privileges of the web server process. This allows the attacker to execute operating system commands, read server-side files including configuration files and database credentials, write files, and reach internal services. In default installations the core:themes:create permission is granted to the Administrator role, and in multi-operator setups it may be delegated to other roles. This is an incomplete fix for GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg.

This allows the attacker to execute operating system commands, read server-side files including configuration files and database credentials, write files, and reach internal services. In default installations the core:themes:create permission is granted to the Administrator role, and in multi-operator setups it may be delegated to other roles. This is an incomplete fix for GHSA-9fx4-7cmj-47vg.

descriptions.description: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. In versions 5.0.0 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, global shortcode expansion runs over the complete rendered page, including HTML-escaped blog comments supplied by unauthenticated visitors. A comment containing the BcBaser.getGoogleMaps shortcode can set apiBaseUrl to an attacker-controlled script URL, which is emitted as a script src and executes JavaScript on the site's origin when another visitor or administrator opens the article displaying that comment. Escaping raw HTML in comments does not prevent this stored cross-site scripting because shortcode processing happens after HTML rendering. Other registered shortcodes also expand in comments; Mail.getForm can embed a working contact form with a valid CSRF token. The flaw can compromise the authenticated browser context of an administrator who views the affected article. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

cna.title: Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl send response bodies for HEAD requests, desynchronizing responses on keep-alive connections

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starman 0.4019 or later.

workarounds.value: For deployments that cannot upgrade to 0.4019, enable Plack::Middleware::Head, which removes the body from HEAD responses.

descriptions.value:
Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl send response bodies for HEAD requests, desynchronizing responses on keep-alive connections.

For a HEAD request Starman omits chunked framing but still writes the body returned by the application, on both the array and streaming response paths. Responses with a 1xx, 204 or 304 status also carry the body.

On a keep-alive or pipelined connection the client reads those bytes as the start of the next response. A front-end proxy that reuses upstream connections may then pair responses with the wrong requests.

Exposed credentials can be used to access the database or other connected services, and anyone with the public asset URL can retrieve the file contents.

descriptions.value: The Prime Mover – Backup and Migration plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 2.2.1 via deserialization of untrusted input in the migration search-and-replace routine (recursiveUnserializeReplace()). An unauthenticated attacker can store a crafted, base64-encoded serialized object in wp_comments.comment_content through the standard comment-submission endpoint (wp-comments-post.php). When an administrator subsequently performs a routine Prime Mover export or restore, the plugin base64-decodes that stored value and passes it to unserialize() with no allowed_classes restriction. A Property-Oriented Programming (POP) chain is present in the plugin's own bundled Freemius library (FS_Clone_Manager::__set → FS_Option_Manager::set_option → store() → update_option()), so no additional plugin or theme is required — the plugin ships the gadget itself.

cna.title: Model Context Protocol Python SDK: OAuth client could send credentials to an authorization server chosen by the MCP server

descriptions.value: The Model Context Protocol Python SDK is the official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients. From 1.9.1 until 1.30.0 and 2.2.0, OAuth client support in mcp.client.auth can send credentials to an authorization server chosen by an untrusted MCP server. ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider cannot identify the authorization server that owns their credentials. Affected HTTP clients using those providers, OAuthClientProvider, or the deprecated 1.x RFC7523OAuthClientProvider can disclose a client_secret, authorization code, PKCE code_verifier, or signed client assertion. MCP servers, stdio clients, and clients that attach their own tokens or headers are not affected. Interactive OAuthClientProvider use requires a person to start sign-in, while the unattended providers do not. For ClientCredentialsOAuthProvider and PrivateKeyJWTOAuthProvider, callers must configure issuer= after upgrading because omission still follows the MCP server's advertised authorization server, and the deprecated RFC7523OAuthClientProvider must be replaced because it has no issuer option. A stored client registration without an issuer remains unbound after upgrading, so stored OAuth client information must be cleared once to register again or a manually pre-registered record must be updated with its issuer. This issue is fixed in versions 1.30.0 and 2.2.0.

cna.title: Apache WSS4J: Replay protection bypassed by concurrent copies of a message

credits.value: This issue was reported independently by Wanxin Yin (MegaVector / yaklang.io) and hataehoon (GitHub: @dpfkdlemtp).

descriptions.value: Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default. The value is now checked and remembered in a single atomic step. Custom ReplayCache implementations should override the new ReplayCache.addIfAbsent method with an operation that is atomic in their underlying store. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.3 or 3.0.7 or 2.4.5, which fix this issue.

cna.title: baserCMS: Mail-form auto-replies accept multiple visitor-controlled recipients

descriptions.value: baserCMS is a website development framework. In versions 5.2.5 before 5.3.2 and 5.4.0 before 5.4.2, an unauthenticated visitor can supply a comma-separated address list in a public mail form's email field and cause a single auto-reply to be addressed to multiple third parties. MailMessageMailer::sendFormToUser() passes the visitor-controlled userMail value to parseAndNormalizeMailAddresses(), which splits it with explode(',') and supplies every resulting address to setTo(). Newly created forms with an email-type field are affected when the separate, optional VALID_EMAIL server-side validation is not enabled; browser type=email validation does not prevent crafted requests. The bundled contact form enables VALID_EMAIL and is not affected. The auto-reply uses the site's sender identity and includes partially attacker-controlled content, allowing abuse of the site to deliver unsolicited mail. This issue has been patched in versions 5.3.2 and 5.4.2.

cna.title: Tornado: Event loop blocking and excess memory use from chunked bodies with many small chunks

descriptions.value: Tornado is a Python web framework and asynchronous networking library. Prior to 6.6.0, Tornado decodes HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding by processing body data that has already arrived without yielding to the event loop. A remote unauthenticated peer can send millions of one-byte chunks to monopolize the process event loop and stall every other connection served by that process, while lowering max_body_size only limits the duration of each request. For handlers that do not use @stream_request_body, retaining each chunk as a separate object can consume roughly twenty times the received body size, and SimpleAsyncHTTPClient has the same event-loop behavior when reading a response from a malicious server. This issue is fixed in version 6.6.0.

descriptions.value: In `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11/v2` versions `<= 2.0.0-rc8` (and the deprecated v1 module paths `github.com/eclipse-keypont/crypto11 <= 1.6.8`, `github.com/ThalesGroup/crypto11 <= 1.7.0-rc1` and `github.com/ThalesIgnite/crypto11 <= 1.2.5`), the `cipher.AEAD` returned by `SecretKey.NewGCM()` passes whatever nonce it is given straight to `CK_GCM_PARAMS` without checking its length against `NonceSize()`, and accepts an empty nonce. On a token that accepts a zero-length GCM IV — SoftHSM2 does — every `Seal` with an empty nonce encrypts under the same IV, reusing the keystream and exposing the GHASH authentication key, which allows forgeries. Separately, `Config.UseGCMIVFromHSM` sends a NULL IV with length zero to the token unless `GCMIVFromHSMControl.SupplyIvForHSMGCMEncrypt` is also set, so the token has nowhere to write the IV it generates: a `Seal` with a non-empty nonce panics after the plaintext has already been encrypted, and a `Seal` with an empty nonce returns ciphertext under an empty IV without error. On the v1 line HSM-IV mode additionally never copies the token-generated IV back to the caller, so the caller keeps its own nonce while the data was encrypted under another one.

descriptions.value: Oversized Serialized Data Payloads

solutions.value: Upgrade APM Server versions 8.3.0 through 8.19.23 to 8.19.24.
Upgrade APM Server versions 9.0.0 through 9.4.8 to 9.4.9.
Upgrade APM Server versions 9.5.0 through 9.5.5 to 9.5.6.

workarounds.value: There are no workarounds for this vulnerability.

descriptions.value:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in APM Server can lead to denial of service via Oversized Serialized Data Payloads (CAPEC-231). An attacker who can send OpenTelemetry (OTLP) data to APM Server over HTTP can cause APM Server to exhaust its memory and terminate. This stops the intake of APM and OpenTelemetry data until APM Server restarts.

The issue is resolved in version 8.19.24, 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. The fixed versions reject OTLP/HTTP requests with a body larger than 64 MiB after decompression, as recommended by the OTLP specification.

cna.title: vLLM: Out-of-vocabulary prompt token id passes input validation and triggers a CUDA device-side assert (engine crash / DoS)

descriptions.value: vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, vllm/tokenizers/hf.py computes max_token_id with an off-by-one upper bound, allowing a pre-tokenized prompt ID equal to the vocabulary size to pass validation. For a tensor-parallel size of one and an exact multiple-of-64 vocabulary, VocabParallelEmbedding.forward does not mask that value before F.embedding uses it, causing a CUDA device-side assertion and terminating the engine. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

descriptions.value: LimeSurvey Community Edition 7.7.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Central Participants Database blocklist control. cna.title: Rembg: Unauthenticated SAM model injection permits local-file disclosure through malicious ONNX graphs

descriptions.value: Rembg is a tool to remove images background. Prior to 2.0.82, the public /api/remove endpoint passes attacker-controlled extras.sam_model through rembg/commands/s_command.py to rembg/sessions/sam.py, where it is interpolated into SAM filenames and GitHub download URLs passed to pooch.retrieve() without a pinned hash. An unauthenticated attacker can supply a sam_model value combining path traversal with URL fragment syntax to exploit the HTTP request discarding the fragment while the local POSIX path retains it. The first request primes the attacker-selected path tree, and an identical repeated request downloads malicious ONNX encoder and decoder files beside a readable target file. The graphs can load the target through ONNX external data and encode its bytes into the returned PNG mask, disclosing complete files accessible to the rembg process and allowing arbitrary ONNX computation. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.82.

cna.title: Electron: Mitigation for compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates

descriptions.value: Electron is a framework for writing cross-platform desktop applications using JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Prior to 42.11.16, 43.8.1, 44.9.1, and 45.0.0-beta.6, Electron does not block compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates in Chromium networking, Node.js tls, Node.js https, or Node.js fetch. An attacker who holds a certificate issued through one of these intermediates and can intercept network traffic can impersonate a TLS server to an affected application. This issue is fixed in versions 42.11.16, 43.8.1, 44.9.1, and 45.0.0-beta.6.

cna.title: One-byte buffer overflow in wide scanf %s and %[ conversions

descriptions.value:
Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

A person with component-management access in a Storyblok space could store a component name containing path traversal sequences; when another user later ran a backup for that space, the stored name escaped the configured backup directory and caused a JSON file to be written outside it on the backup host. cna.title: Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded buffering of chunked request bodies

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starman 0.4019 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded buffering of chunked request bodies.

The chunked body decoder keeps each chunk in memory until the whole chunk and its CRLF have arrived, and sets no limit on the length of a chunk-size line. A client that declares a huge chunk size and streams data, or sends a chunk-size line that never ends, grows the buffer for as long as it keeps sending.

A remote attacker can exhaust worker memory with a single connection.

cna.title: Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic regex backtracking when parsing chunked request bodies

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starman 0.4019 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic regex backtracking when parsing chunked request bodies.

Starman decodes chunked request bodies before calling the application, matching each chunk-size line with `s/^(([0-9a-fA-F]+).*\015\012)//`. A line of hex digits followed by a bare LF and then CRLF never matches, because `.` does not match LF, and each failed attempt backtracks in time quadratic in the length of the hex run. Nothing limits the length of the line.

A remote attacker can exhaust worker CPU by sending such requests to any route.

solutions.value: Upgrade to Plack 1.0057 or later.

descriptions.value:
HTTP::Server::PSGI versions before 1.0056 for Perl allow a single request to crash the server by declaring a large Content-Length.

The request body is read with sysread() calls sized by the remaining Content-Length. Perl grows the read buffer to the requested length before any data arrives, so the server tries to allocate as much memory as the client declares.

A remote attacker can send one request with a large Content-Length and a few body bytes, and perl exits with an out-of-memory error before the application is called. HTTP::Server::PSGI runs as a single process, so the server stays down until restarted.

From 0.19.0 until 0.32.0, authenticated callers can supply a request chat template when no server-side --chat-template is configured, or a malicious model repository can provide a template that is compiled and rendered by tokenizer.apply_chat_template() without a wall-clock timeout, output-size limit, or iteration bound. Rendering runs in a ThreadPoolExecutor with one worker by default, so a nonterminating render can block /v1/responses and other chat-template users after the request ends, while an output-expanding render can exhaust server memory. Harmony models are not affected because they do not use this Jinja path. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

cna.title: Monoceros versions before 0.30 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory

solutions.value: Upgrade to Monoceros 0.30 or later.

descriptions.value:
Monoceros versions before 0.30 for Perl allow a request declaring a large Content-Length to kill a worker by exhausting memory.

The request body is read in a loop that asks sysread for all of the remaining declared length at once. Perl grows the read buffer to that size before any data arrives, so a length larger than available memory makes the worker exit with an uncatchable out of memory error before the application is called.

A remote attacker can force a worker restart with each request of a few bytes.

cna.title: Ipa: freeipa: freeipa uses subject cn as proof of certificate ownership

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Andrew Rukin (Arenadata) for reporting this issue.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in FreeIPA. An improper authorization check allows an authenticated host to retrieve and revoke digital certificates assigned to other users or services. This issue occurs because FreeIPA verifies ownership solely by matching the host name to the certificate's subject Common Name (CN), without confirming actual ownership in the directory service. Consequently, an enrolled host can disrupt services by revoking certificates belonging to other entities.

cna.title: LangGraph: Namespace labels containing `.` reach other namespaces in Postgres and SQLite stores

descriptions.value: LangGraph checkpoint savers provide Postgres- and SQLite-backed state persistence for LangGraph workflows and agents. Prior to langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2, PostgresStore, AsyncPostgresStore, SqliteStore, and AsyncSqliteStore flatten namespace labels with ".".join(namespace), while BaseStore validates labels only for put and aput. Unvalidated dotted labels passed through get, search, delete, list_namespaces, their asynchronous equivalents, or direct batch and abatch operations can resolve to another tenant's stored namespace, allowing cross-namespace reads, overwrites, or deletion. InMemoryStore is not affected because it compares namespace tuples. This issue is fixed in langgraph-checkpoint-postgres 3.1.3 and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite 3.1.2.

descriptions.value: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) in the cart and wishlist repositories of MarcosCamara01 Ecommerce Template allows any authenticated user to delete and modify the cart and wishlist rows of any other user, because cartRepository.delete(), cartRepository.updateQuantityInternal() and wishlistRepository.delete() in src/lib/db/drizzle/repositories/ match rows by primary key alone, with no predicate on the owning user, and the per user authorization for those three operations rests on PostgreSQL row level security. The migrations run ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and create policies comparing app.current_user_id() with user_id, but never ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, and PostgreSQL does not apply policies to the role that owns a table. The template uses one DATABASE_URL both to run the migrations, which create the tables, and for the application at runtime, so the application connects as the owner of the tables and the policies do not apply to it. cart_items.id and wishlist.id are sequential bigserial values, so the identifiers of rows belonging to other users can be enumerated, and the update path returns the modified row, which carries the identifier of the user it belongs to. This results in the destruction and modification of cart and wishlist contents belonging to other accounts of the installation.

cna.title: Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow a stalled request body to hold a worker indefinitely, as read_timeout covers only the headers

solutions.value: Upgrade to Starman 0.4019 or later.

descriptions.value:
Starman versions before 0.4019 for Perl allow a stalled request body to hold a worker indefinitely, as read_timeout covers only the headers.

Content-Length and chunked request bodies are read with blocking reads and no deadline. A client that sends complete headers and then stalls or trickles the body keeps the worker waiting until it disconnects.

A remote attacker can take every worker with a few such connections, five with the default worker count, so the server stops answering requests.

Version 0.4019 applies read_timeout to each wait for body data and adds a body_timeout limit, 300 seconds by default, on the total time to read a body.

cna.title: Oc: oc: symlink/hardlink target validation bypass in oc image extract allows file write outside destination

credits.value: Red Hat would like to thank Yashashree Gund for reporting this issue.

workarounds.value:
Treat container images as trusted inputs when using oc image extract. Do not extract images from registries or publishers you do not control or have not verified.

Where possible, run oc image extract as an unprivileged user and into a dedicated, isolated destination directory, and avoid fixed/predictable destination paths in automated or CI pipelines. Restrict who can modify the image references that automated extraction jobs consume.

There is no configuration option to disable only this link-extraction behavior. Apply updated oc client packages or rebuilt platform images when Red Hat publishes them for your product and stream.

descriptions.value: A flaw was found in the OpenShift client oc. When extracting container image layers with oc image extract, the application fails to properly sanitize symbolic and hard link targets pointing to absolute paths or to sibling directories of the extraction destination. An attacker who supplies a malicious container image can exploit this vulnerability by embedding links, and a chained file entry, that reference locations outside the intended extraction directory. This allows the attacker to write attacker-controlled content to arbitrary locations on the host filesystem with the privileges of the user running the command, potentially leading to file modification outside the destination directory.

descriptions.value: MLflow is an open source AI engineering platform for agents, large language models, and machine learning models. From 3.12.0rc0 until 3.17.0, the scorer invoke, register, and GenAI evaluate endpoints, including unauthenticated POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/scorer/invoke, accept serialized third-party scorer data that Scorer.model_validate_json resolves using a module-path allowlist without constraining the selected class or its constructor arguments. When optional trulens and trulens-providers-litellm packages are installed, an attacker can select mlflow.genai.scorers.trulens, choose a model URI outside MLflow's native provider registry so execution uses the LiteLLM fallback, and supply api_base and api_key values that cause the server to send an outbound request to an attacker-chosen or internal host with attacker-controlled headers and body. The vulnerable deserialization occurs before a tracking-store lookup or job submission. This issue is fixed in version 3.17.0.

cna.title: imaplib STARTTLS serves plaintext bytes buffered before the handshake as if they came over TLS

descriptions.value: IMAP4.starttls() wraps the socket in TLS but leaves self._readbuf, imaplib's own read-ahead buffer, untouched. Any plaintext bytes that arrived in the same recv() as the tagged OK to STARTTLS are returned by readline() after the handshake, so the client treats them as the first responses on the protected channel. A network attacker who cannot break TLS can append forged lines after the server's OK, let the handshake complete with the real server and a valid certificate, and have the client accept the forged CAPABILITY and the forged tagged completion of the next command. This is the STARTTLS command/response injection class of CVE-2011-0411.

cna.title: Path traversal in post media lets any registered user read server files

descriptions.value: Where the Discord provider is configured, any registered user can read any regular file the publishing worker can read and have it delivered byte for byte to a Discord server they control.

Files within reach include those that hold the JWT signing secret, the database address and provider client secrets, such as the instance's environment file, mounted secret files and application logs, and the worker's process environment.

A second route lets a user with a connected Dribbble, TikTok or Pinterest channel learn whether a path exists and whether it is a file or a directory, and exhaust the backend's memory with one request by pointing at a device file, which stops the backend from answering any organization until it is killed.
A third route, on instances using local storage with an empty cloud bucket URL, reaches the same file read without needing a WordPress site.

exploits.value: Exploitation was demonstrated end to end against unmodified builds of the backend and the orchestrator at commit 3a7d28b7ad96, using only a self-registered account: a file outside the upload directory arrived byte for byte as an attachment in the attacker's Discord channel. The validation-time route and the stored media route were also exercised separately against the same builds.

timeline.value: Anthropic has disclosed a thorough report of this vulnerability including a working PoC to Postiz
Postiz has reproduced the vulnerability and is working on a fix
Postiz has pushed a fix for this vulnerability and verified it
Postiz has created a release and published the advisory

workarounds.value: Set DISABLE_REGISTRATION=true. The attacker needs an ordinary account, so closing self-registration limits exposure to people who already hold one. This reduces reach, it does not close the issue.
If you do not need the Discord provider, leave its client id, client secret and bot token unset. This removes the main route only; the other routes remain.

descriptions.value:
When a post is published, Postiz treats a media path that is not a web address as a file on the server's disk, but it does not check that the file lies inside the upload directory. A registered user can store a crafted media path with a post, get it past the checks that normally restrict it, and have the publishing worker read an arbitrary file and send it as an attachment to a Discord server the user controls.

The same unconfined reads can be reached through two further routes. One tells the caller whether a file exists and can exhaust the backend's memory, the other delivers the file the same way as the main route. Self-registration is open by default, so the attacker needs no existing account.

configurations.value: The main route requires the Discord provider to be enabled, that is DISCORD_CLIENT_ID, DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET and DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN_ID set. These are empty in the shipped docker-compose.yaml. The storage provider does not matter.
The validation-time route requires a Dribbble, TikTok or Pinterest provider to be configured.
The shipped container runs the worker as root, so every file root can read is exposed. Self-registration is open unless DISABLE_REGISTRATION is set to true.

cna.title: Mongoose: Heap OOB reads and null-byte bypass in mg_path_is_sane (util.c)

descriptions.value: Mongoose is an embedded web server and network library. Prior to 7.22, mg_path_is_sane in src/util.c read path.buf[1] without first requiring path.len to be at least two and read s[2] when only two bytes remained. Unauthenticated remote requests reaching mg_http_upload or mg_http_serve_dir with the affected short path shapes could therefore trigger one-byte heap out-of-bounds reads. On bare-metal or RTOS targets without memory protection, the adjacent byte could be exposed or influence whether a path was accepted, and instrumented builds could crash. This issue is fixed in version 7.22.

@fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

cna.title: Docker Engine overlay-network encryption rules are not restored after a firewalld reload

descriptions.value: An affected node sends encrypted overlay-network traffic in cleartext, exposing container traffic to observers on the network path between nodes. An attacker able to send UDP datagrams to the node's VXLAN port (by default, UDP port 4789) can inject arbitrary Ethernet frames into an encrypted overlay network. On releases with the fix for CVE-2026-92542, a process in the host network namespace with CAP_NET_RAW can also have its own VXLAN datagrams encrypted using the node's IPsec security associations. Traffic between affected nodes continues in cleartext, while nodes that retain their encryption rules discard cleartext datagrams from affected peers, disrupting communication without preventing the cleartext exposure.

workarounds.value: Configure firewalld to preserve other applications' iptables rules: use FirewallBackend=nftables with a build that includes commit b7faa74db15e2d1ebd9fdfcdc7579874d3a2fa87 (firewalld 2.0.0 or later, or the RHEL backports listed in configurations), and remove all firewalld direct configuration. Alternatively, restart dockerd after every firewalld reload, stop, or start to restore the encryption rules; this also restarts the node's Swarm tasks. As defense in depth, block incoming traffic to the VXLAN port (by default, UDP port 4789) at the Internet boundary. This prevents injection from outside the boundary but does not protect the confidentiality of traffic between nodes.

descriptions.value: Moby's overlay network driver does not restore the iptables rules for encrypted overlay networks after firewalld deletes them. Unlike other Docker Engine networking components, the overlay driver does not handle firewalld reload or start signals over D-Bus. The missing rules cause outgoing VXLAN datagrams to bypass IPsec encryption and remove the protection against incoming cleartext VXLAN traffic. The condition is not logged by dockerd and persists until the encrypted network's last local endpoint is removed and another is added, or dockerd is restarted. Each further firewalld event repeats the condition.

configurations.value: Linux Swarm nodes with at least one task or container attached to an encrypted overlay network, running firewalld in a configuration that deletes other applications' iptables rules. This includes FirewallBackend=iptables in any firewalld version. With FirewallBackend=nftables, a node is affected if firewalld lacks commit b7faa74db15e2d1ebd9fdfcdc7579874d3a2fa87 (included in firewalld 2.0.0 and later, firewalld-1.2.5-1.el9 for RHEL 9, and firewalld-0.9.11-9.el8 for RHEL 8), or if firewalld has direct rules, direct chains, or tracked passthrough rules. The FlushAllOnReload setting does not determine whether a node is affected. Rules are deleted on firewalld reload or complete reload, on stop with CleanupOnExit=yes (the default), and on start, including restart or starting firewalld after dockerd.

references.name: AshPostgres ignores attribute multitenancy on the join resource when loading `many_to_many` and `through` relationships, returning records related through other tenants' rows

descriptions.value:
Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in ash-project ash_postgres allows a user to load destination records linked to a source record only through another tenant's join rows.

When a many_to_many relationship, or a through relationship, is loaded with a lateral join (for example with a per-record limit or sort), AshPostgres.DataLayer builds the query for the join resource, and for each resource along a through path, in lateral_join_query/3 and through_step_queries/4 without running that resource's read action, which is where attribute multitenancy is applied. When those resources use strategy :attribute multitenancy, rows belonging to other tenants were joined, so the load returned destination records that the caller's tenant is not related to.

This issue affects ash_postgres: from 0.38.0 before 2.15.2.

descriptions.description: CWE-129: Improper Validation of Array Index

descriptions.value: Go-Guerrilla SMTP Daemon is a lightweight SMTP server written in Go. In 1.6.7 and earlier, according to the repository advisory's structured affected range, server.go defines the seven-byte cmdXCLIENT token, but the XCLIENT handler slices input[8:] after matching only that seven-byte verb, so a bare command causes an out-of-bounds panic in handleClient and terminates the daemon because that connection goroutine does not recover the panic. The issue is reachable by an unauthenticated client when the non-default xclient_on setting is enabled; no HELO command is required. The repository fix is present in version 1.6.7-1.
